Implemented compound_assign fixup: rewrites 'a = a <op> rhs' -> 'a <op>= rhs' for simple local slots with pure rhs. Added Stmt::CompoundAssign to Rust AST. Verified with cargo fmt + cargo nextest r --release (136 passed).

Lowered the cir.libc.mem* family (memcpy/memmove/memset/memchr) to byte-wise std::ptr ops + __slate_memchr helper; added PtrCopy/WriteBytes AST nodes and 4 differential fixtures. Plain libc mem* calls already worked via extern; only clang builtins/aggregate bit_cast raise these ops. Idiom-recognizer is a no-op stub upstream (noted in emit.rs).

Added call_args rust_ast fixup: inlines single-use temps into (a) declared param slots of non-variadic callees and (b) call-result temps into any slot (incl. vararg) when no side effect sits between def and use. Vararg bare-literal hazard stays blocked. add.c now emits add(2,3)/add(-10,4)/add(0,0) with results handed directly to printf. 4 unit tests + differential shape assertion; cargo fmt + nextest (141) green.

Implemented conservative retval fixup for main exit boilerplate in src/fixups/retval.rs, added differential output-shape coverage, and verified with cargo fmt, cargo test, and cargo nextest r --release.

Added drop_call_results fixup: drops the binding of a synthetic _vN temp that holds an unused call result, rewriting 'let _v = <call>;' to a bare '<call>;' (preserving unsafe wrappers and arg evaluation). Only call-bearing inits are touched; used results and pure unused temps are left alone. Unusedness checked per lexical scope incl. block tails. compound_assignments/add.c now emit 'unsafe { printf(...) };'. 4 unit tests + differential shape assertion; integrated with slate-04q.5 (retval sig change) at merge; cargo fmt + nextest (149) green.

Rendered control-flow conditions (if/let-if/match/expr-if/expr-match) bare instead of at PREC_CALL, matching Stmt::While; the precedence-aware renderer already emitted minimal arithmetic/bitwise/shift parens so no AST paren node existed to strip. Added redundant_parens.c fixture + assertion test.

Implemented remove_mut fixup over Rust AST bindings: removes mut from params/locals without later mutation, preserves mut for assignments, address-taking, mutable borrows, array mutable pointers, atomics, and method receivers. Added unit and differential shape coverage. Verified with cargo fmt, cargo test, stdlib_coverage, generated_differential, and cargo nextest r --release.

Implemented AST printf format recovery for constant formats with plain text, %%, and one or more %d conversions; all-or-nothing per program to avoid mixed stdout buffering; removes printf extern when fully rewritten. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release.

Extended printf macro recovery to %i, %u, %ld, %lu, %lld, %llu, and %zu constant integer formats with exact argument counts. Added unit and differential output-shape coverage. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release.

Implemented conservative static integer printf width/flag recovery for zero padding, left alignment, plus signs, and static widths; rejects dynamic widths, precision, space/# flags, and ambiguous combinations. Added unit tests plus printf_integer_widths differential fixture. Verified cargo fmt in the ticket worktree and cargo nextest r --release on main; main cargo fmt --check is currently blocked by unrelated dirty preprocessor edits.

Added preprocessing oracle (src/preprocess.rs) recording #if/#ifdef/#ifndef/#elif/#else/#endif regions with normalized predicates, directive/body source ranges, mapped Rust cfgs, and active/inactive state resolved against Clang's predefined macros. Unknown predicates are kept opaque + diagnosed, not guessed. Exposed via 'record-cfg' JSON command; recorded cfgs match tests/fixtures.cfg/expected_cfgs.json. Existing single-config/translate-cfg behavior unchanged. Verified with cargo nextest r --release (183 tests).

Implemented conservative printf %s/%c macro recovery for direct constant UTF-8 C strings and constant ASCII character values, with local constant tracking and rejection of pointer strings, interior-NUL strings, and non-ASCII character bytes. Added unit tests plus supported/rejected differential fixtures. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release on main.

Implemented fixed-decimal printf macro recovery for %f and %.Nf in src/fixups/printf_format.rs, with supported and rejected fixtures. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release on main (187 passed).

Rewrote translate-cfg to derive the whole-item cfg matrix from the lq0.2 preprocessing oracle instead of a filename table: each recorded branch -> a variant with clang args pinning every chain macro, rust_cfg from the recorded predicate mapping, validated against the oracle to activate exactly its branch. OS/arch/NDEBUG fixture output is unchanged. Refuses with diagnostics: fragment cuts inside a function/record body (brace-depth scan), predicates without a known cfg mapping, and >1 top-level chain (nested/sibling deferred). No-conditional sources pass through to single-config lowering (unchanged). Known limitation: negated/ifndef opening branches are validation-refused rather than merged (candidate uses a define-atoms heuristic); multi/nested chains deferred per epic scope. Added reject fixtures + tests. Verified cargo nextest r --release (195 tests) and cargo fmt.
emit-fixtures now renders tests/fixtures.cfg/*.c through translate-cfg into git-ignored tests/fixtures.cfg.generated/*.rs (reject/ skipped) for side-by-side C/Rust comparison.

Added docs/cfg-portability.md: single-config vs multi-config semantics, the supported predicate->cfg table (_WIN32/__linux__/__APPLE__/x86_64/aarch64/arm/NDEBUG), user macro configs via SLATE_CLANG_ARGS + record-cfg, and refusal cases. Linked from CLAUDE.md and cfg fixtures README.

Implemented printf %x/%X/%o macro recovery in src/fixups/printf_format.rs, including static width, zero padding, and left alignment forms. Added printf_hex_octal fixture and differential output-shape assertions. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release on main (196 passed).

Added rust_ast::Cfg (Flag/Opt/Not/Any/All) + Item::Cfg wrapper, rendered by codegen. preprocess::pred_to_cfg now builds Cfg values (Branch.rust_cfg: Option<Cfg>); cfg_translate merges/gates whole rust_ast Items via item_key, dropping all text-splitting. #[cfg(...)] now emitted from the AST, not a formatted string. Output byte-for-byte unchanged; 196 tests pass.

Added printf_alternate_integer fixture and differential output-shape assertions. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release on main (197 passed).

Implemented conservative printf %p recovery in src/fixups/printf_format.rs with pointer-typed argument checks, supported/rejected fixtures, and output-shape assertions. Verified with cargo test --test differential -- --nocapture and cargo nextest r --release.

Dispatch-loop break mismatch fixed: value-returning functions emit unreachable!() at the wildcard so the loop diverges and coerces to the return type; verified in isolation and on regenerated libyaml crate (no E0308 dispatch errors).
Implemented AST string_lift fixup with structural &str/&[u8] Rust AST types, conservative raw-pointer safety checks, and differential coverage. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release.

Fixed in inline_temps fixup: single_safe_use ignored the enclosing block's yielded tail (LetIf then_value/else_value, unsafe block tail), so a temp used once in the body and once in the yielded value was wrongly inlined, dangling the tail reference (E0425 _vN). Threaded tails into the use analysis; temps feeding a tail keep their binding. Verified on regenerated libyaml crate: 0 missing-value errors (was _v279 in scanner.rs). Added fixture assign_value_in_branch.c + unit test; 219 tests pass.

Implemented a post-string-lift AST fixup for strlen/strcmp/strncmp/memcmp on lifted &str/&[u8] operands, with conservative interdependent lifting and differential coverage. Verified with cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release.

Fixed stale extern cleanup for the string_libc fixup: rewritten strlen/strcmp/strncmp/memcmp declarations are now pruned when no raw calls remain, while surviving raw calls keep their externs. Verified generated fixture output plus cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release.

Emit typedef'd anonymous records (yaml_string_t) via typedef-name adoption in c_ast, and function-local anonymous structs (anon.N STACK/QUEUE locals) synthesized from CIR type-alias layout + get_member field names, emitted per-module. libyaml crate 'cannot find type' errors: 58 -> 0. Remaining crate errors are unrelated signedness/field mismatches.

Adjusted lifted strlen rewrites to keep Rust's native usize result: generated temps now use usize and assign s.len() directly instead of u64 plus as u64. Verified fixture output plus cargo fmt and cargo nextest r --release.

Built a typedef table from Clang AST TypedefDecl nodes; parse_c_type resolves pointer/array-to-typedef base names through it before substring inference. yaml_char_t* now maps to *mut u8 matching CIR. libyaml crate E0308: 3956 -> 501 (remainder are i32/u32 enum mismatches = q0g.6). Fixture tests/fixtures/typedef_ptr_signedness.c guards the regression. Merged to main; 222/222 tests pass.

Implemented a string_copy AST fixup for safe local char buffers, rewriting unused strcpy/strncpy/strcat/strncat to String to_owned/push_str forms with truncating n-variant coverage. Verified with cargo fmt && cargo nextest r --release.

Added src/fixups/support/walk.rs read-only AST traversal helpers, migrated existing fixup walkers and string_copy boilerplate to use them, and documented the helpers in docs/writing-a-fixup.md. Verified with cargo fmt && cargo nextest r --release.

collect_records dropped the recursion (continue) after naming an anonymous record, so nested anonymous records (yaml_event_s.data.alias/.tag structs, node data variants) were emitted empty and field accesses hit E0609. Fall through to recurse. libyaml crate E0609: 333->0 (also E0308 74->40 from downstream). Fixture nested_anon_struct_fields.c guards it; 227/227 pass. Merged to main.
Added override-style expr/stmt fixup AST walkers in src/fixups/support/walk.rs, documented them, and verified with cargo fmt && cargo nextest r --release.

Member/element access with a bare raw-pointer-value base (e.g. (*p).f) computed unsafe_access without accounting for the base deref, so stores '(*p).f = x' and 'addr_of_mut!((*p).f)' args were emitted outside unsafe -> E0133. Mark unsafe_access when base is dereferenced (place_expr None) and wrap addr-of in unsafe when unsafe. libyaml crate E0133: 1864->0. Fixture ptr_member_store_unsafe.c guards it; 232/232 pass. Merged to main.

Found two distinct bugs, both fixed in src/lower.rs's lower_get_element/global_array_literal_expr: (1) indexing a narrow string literal (e.g. "abc"[0]) decayed the backing global to a single-char pointer before indexing, producing a type error (indexing i8); (2) indexing a wide/concatenated string literal (L""/u"", or narrow+wide concatenation) referenced a const-array global that wasn't in the 'strings' byte map, falling through to a raw unsanitized identifier (e.g. '(*.str.60)[0]') -- a syntax error. Fixed by rendering the backing global as an inline array literal (correctly padded to its declared CIR length, since trailing_zeros initializers omit the padding) and indexing that directly instead of decaying through a pointer. A third, unrelated bug surfaced once those were fixed: stdout line ordering vs C, caused by mixing println! (immediate flush) with raw libc printf (flushes only at exit) across translation units -- fixed in src/fixups/rewrite/printf_format.rs and tracked/documented on slate-pcek.10 since it also unblocked 9 other unsupported fixtures. string.c promoted to tests/fixtures.chibicc/supported/.

Result threaded onto Function.macro_consts (Vec<String>, source order) and consumed positionally in lower.rs the same way layout_queries already handles sizeof/alignof. This unblocked slate-04q.60's full limits.h scope, including the small/ambiguous values (SCHAR_MIN, UCHAR_MAX, CHAR_BIT) originally excluded there.

In lower.rs: FunctionLowerer.macro_consts (VecDeque<String>, source order, from c_ast.rs's Function.macro_consts) is consumed positionally at two points -- next_macro_const_expr() at cir.const (handles single-literal macros like INT_MAX), and a fold-and-check added to lower_int_arith() (handles multi-op macros like INT_MIN's cir.sub or UINT_MAX's cir.mul+cir.add, via a small macro_arith_values side-table chained onto const_int_values). Both only substitute when the *folded numeric value* also matches the confirmed macro's known value, so a coincidental value match without the plugin's confirmation is never enough on its own.

pointer_neg promoted to supported/. alignof substantially closer but not fully promoted -- split remaining blocker to slate-04q.62 (see below), matching this ticket's acceptance criteria allowance for unrelated width-mismatch bugs.

Root cause of the originally-cited '_N vs _vN unresolved reference' and 'offset_from receiver/signedness' bugs: three CIR ops -- lower_ptr_stride, lower_ptr_diff, and the array-decay-to-integer arm of lower_cast -- called operand_expr() (which only resolves self.values/self.slots) on a pointer-typed base that was actually an ElementPtr/MemberPtr fact (never materialized into self.values), or applied no cast at all when a pointer decayed to a plain integer result type. Fixed by:
  - lower_ptr_stride/lower_ptr_diff: use pointer_operand_expr() instead of operand_expr() for pointer-typed operands, so element/member place facts resolve to a real std::ptr::addr_of_mut!(...) expression instead of falling through to a bare, unresolved SSA-name identifier.
  - lower_cast: two related ptrtoint bugs found and fixed in the same investigation -- (1) a Global operand cast to a non-pointer result type was passed through unresolved as Val::Global, which a later to_expr() rendered as a bare read of the global's VALUE (e.g. '(long)&g1 % 512' became 'g1 % 512', silently reading g1's stored contents instead of its address); (2) a local array slot decaying to a non-pointer (integer) result type produced '.as_mut_ptr()' with no enclosing cast, which doesn't type-check against an integer-typed destination. Both now correctly emit 'std::ptr::addr_of!(name) as T' / '(x.as_mut_ptr() as T)'.

Remaining, distinct blocker for alignof (NOT related to the above): repeated GNU statement-expression result temps that Clang's CIR names identically ('tmp') but allocates as separate, differently-typed SSA slots collide in Slate's lower_alloca (no name-collision detection), so Rust's own let-shadowing silently misdirects an earlier binding's reads/writes onto a later, wrong-typed one -- a genuine E0308 in the generated Rust. Filed as slate-04q.62 with a minimal repro and precise root cause; requires its own careful fix (mint a disambiguated name on collision) without disturbing legitimate nested-scope name reuse elsewhere, so intentionally out of scope here.

Verified: cargo fmt, cargo clippy, cargo nextest r --release -- 684/684 passing, including chibicc_supported_tests_match_c (pointer_neg's C/Rust stdout+exit match).

Root cause: Clang CIR hoists all local allocas to a function's entry block, reusing generic compiler names (e.g. 'tmp') across distinct temps such as per-GNU-statement-expression result slots. lower_alloca took the CIR name verbatim, so colliding allocas produced repeated 'let mut tmp = ...' bindings that Rust resolved to the last (differently-typed) shadow, causing widespread i32/u64 call-site mismatches. Fixed by deduping local names per function in src/lower.rs (declared_local_names + unique_local_name). Promoted arith, decl, enum, macro to supported/. bitfield/cast/commonsym/usualconv/typeof still fail but from unrelated causes (anonymous-type naming collisions -- tracked in slate-pcek.8; unsafe/safe fn-pointer coercion in threads.c; a preprocessor-stage C-compile error in typeof.c) -- not part of this cluster.

Same root cause as slate-pcek.4, fixed by the same commit: lower_alloca (src/lower.rs) now dedupes local names per function via a new declared_local_names set / unique_local_name() helper, so distinct hoisted allocas sharing a CIR-generated name (e.g. multiple GNU statement-expression 'tmp' temps) get suffixed (tmp, tmp2, tmp3, ...) instead of colliding into one Rust binding. Verified against this ticket's minimal repro (long/unsigned long statement-expr mix -- now type-checks and returns a==5, b==6) and alignof.c (previously 36 E0308 errors from tmp collisions, now builds clean with zero). Full nextest suite (684 tests) stayed green, including cases with legitimate same-named nested-scope locals, so no shadowing regression. alignof.c still fails end-to-end on an unrelated _Alignas layout bug -- filed separately as slate-pcek.15.

Root cause: cir.global's #cir.global_view<@target> initializer was only handled when target was a string literal (self.strings); a pointer global initialized to another data global's address (Tree *tree = &(Tree){...}) was silently dropped, and the same gap inside render_const_value_expr defaulted struct pointer fields with a global_view initializer (nested compound literals' lhs/rhs) to null. Fixed via a shared global_view_init_expr helper in src/lower.rs, restricted to Type::Ptr targets so it doesn't misfire on non-pointer global_view uses (e.g. a function address stored in an Option<fn> static). Also extended slate-pcek.4's per-function local-name dedup to check against already-collected global names, fixing the E0530 'let binding shadows a static' where a block-scope compound-literal temp reused a file-scope compound-literal static's generated name. Promoted complit to supported/.

Same root cause as slate-pcek.5, fixed by the same commit: collect_global's #cir.global_view<@target> handling silently dropped pointer globals whose target was another data global rather than a string literal, so int *ext2 = &ext1; (common.c) was never inserted into self.globals and thus never registered in defined_globals -- translate-project's cross-module import logic had nothing to point crate::common::ext2 at, hence E0432. Now goes through global_view_init_expr (addr_of_mut!(ext1) as *mut i32), so ext2 is a real global and the cross-module import resolves. Verified end-to-end: extern.c now promotes to supported/ alongside complit.c. No separate tests/fixtures.multi/ regression fixture added -- extern.c exercises this exact shape and stays in the differential suite.

Root cause: collect_anon_record_info (src/lower.rs) only added an anon struct/union type to the 'needed' set when it appeared directly as an alloca's pointee type or a cir.get_member's container type. Two shapes fell through and were referenced-but-never-defined: (1) a record whose only use is as a NESTED FIELD inside another already-needed anon record (e.g. union{struct{...} c;}'s inner struct), fixed with a fixpoint closure over each needed record's expanded field types; (2) a record used only as a top-level GLOBAL's type (cir.global's sym_type, no alloca/get_member at all), fixed by adding a CirOpKind::Global case to the walker. Also fixed a second, unrelated cause hitting the same fixture: cir_type_to_ctype had no !cir.array<...> branch, so an anon record field of array type silently defaulted to scalar i32. Once nested anon types got pulled in, a sibling gap surfaced in the anonymous_structs fixup (same shape of bug, one layer up): renaming a record to a tuple struct only rewrote its own declaration, never sibling records' field types or chained/global field-access expressions referencing it -- fixed by making rewrite_item always walk field types and giving the fixup a record-field-type + global-variable-type table so it can resolve chained access (x._tmp.a, g45.a) through a renamed sibling type. union.c promotes to supported/ and passes end-to-end. bitfield.c's literal 'cannot find type anon_0' is gone, but it hits a separate, deeper issue -- its anonymous bitfield-backed global never gets real a/b/c member names anywhere in the pipeline (unlike a named local bitfield struct, which has dedicated bitfield-aware lowering) -- filed as slate-pcek.16, not the same root cause as this ticket.

Two real bugs found and fixed during verification (manual instrumentation in fixups/mod.rs's RangeLoop step, gated behind SLATE_VERIFY_SPLICE=1, comparing splice_function output against a fresh facts::analyze() after normalizing BindingId/LoopId to (function,name/kind,path) keys - since those IDs are opaque per-snapshot and never compared across FixupFacts instances in production):

1. BindingId/LoopId collision on splice: Collector previously assigned new IDs via Vec::len(), which is only safe for pure-append construction. purge_function_facts's retain() leaves holes mid-Vec, so a post-removal .len() could collide with an existing higher ID belonging to an unrelated, untouched function. Fixed with a new Collector::resume() constructor that computes next_binding/next_loop as a true max(existing_id)+1 (O(n), paid once per splice, not per push). push_function is deliberately left .len()-based since splice_function never calls it - noted as a constraint for any future incremental function-insertion work.

2. Verification harness bug (not in splice_function itself): when one apply() touched multiple functions in a single batch, the original verification loop spliced only one function per iteration into a fresh facts.clone() while comparing against a fully-edited fresh analyze - so other touched-but-not-yet-spliced functions in that same clone read as stale mismatches. Fixed by splicing every touched function into the same clone before the single comparison against one fresh analyze.

Found and fixed a real bug while building this: the LazySingleton step's touched.in_place item_index values are pre-edit indices (get_value's function item_index, recorded before its guard-flag static gets deleted), but the flag deletion shifts every later item's position in the already-mutated post-edit Program. Splicing in-place edits before applying remove_items looked up the wrong (shifted) item out of the post-edit program - e.g. spliced get_value's facts with main's actual body. Fixed by reordering the check to call remove_items first (which shifts the cloned facts' own item_index bookkeeping to match), then resolve/splice in-place items - splice_function reads the current item_index off its own facts snapshot, not a stale pre-edit one. This is a real correctness constraint for .8.4's production wiring, not just a diagnostic-harness artifact - documented in matcher-plan.md section 5.

Wired incremental facts into fixups/mod.rs's production pipeline, but only where it's actually safe - not uniformly across all six migrated steps, per the ticket's own design note to verify the win applies before claiming it.

Audited all six currently-migrated steps (AnonymousStructs, MemchrPreludeFixupCalls, MemchrPrelude, RangeLoop, LibcExit, PruneUnusedDefinitions, plus LazySingleton) for "external facts::analyze immediately follows this step, with no intervening legacy pass." Only one qualifies:

- LazySingleton: plan.apply is directly followed by an external facts::analyze with nothing else in between. apply_with_logger now captures the step's report.touched as its result; when the step ran and !touched.unbounded, the next `facts` binding is built via a new shared splice_incremental_facts helper (FixupFacts::remove_items then splice_function per touched item) instead of a fresh facts::analyze. Falls back to full reanalyze when the step didn't run (debug-mode --only-pass/--up-to-pass filtering) or reported unbounded (never happens for LazySingleton in practice, but handled for safety).

RangeLoop looked like a second candidate but isn't safe when it matters: its step body calls late_loop_cleanup (a legacy pass: SingletonScopes/DeadLocals) whenever report.changed, and that legacy pass walks and can mutate every function in the program, not just the ones StmtWindowPlan::apply reported as touched. Splicing only the reported items in that case would leave late_loop_cleanup's untracked mutations stale - a real correctness bug, not just a missed optimization. So the wiring only splices when late_loop_cleanup did NOT run (!report.changed, where splicing an empty touched set is a no-op); whenever late_loop_cleanup does run, `facts` falls back to a full reanalyze exactly as before.

The other five migrated steps don't have an external analyze to skip at all: MemchrPreludeFixupCalls/MemchrPrelude/LibcExit each call facts::analyze internally within their own step body (nothing external follows immediately); AnonymousStructs has several legacy passes (ParamSpills, ZeroInit, StructFieldInit, SingletonScopes) running before the next external analyze, plus its edits are always TouchedItems::unbounded anyway; PruneUnusedDefinitions is the pipeline's last step, nothing follows it to skip. All of these, and every other legacy rewrite::* pass's facts::analyze call, are unchanged.

Added the IncrementalFacts type to src/fixups/mod.rs: a FixupFacts plus a Dirty marker enum (Clean, Touched(query::TouchedItems), Everything).

- mark_touched(&mut self, touched: &TouchedItems): unbounded touches or an already-Everything state escalate/stay at Everything; otherwise merges into the existing Touched set (or starts one) via TouchedItems::merge. Cheap, never recomputes.
- mark_everything_dirty(&mut self): sets Everything unconditionally.
- resolve(&mut self, program: &Program) -> FixupFacts: the only place recompute happens. Clean is a no-op, Touched(set) reuses the existing splice_incremental_facts helper (remove_items then splice_function per item, exactly the logic .8.4 already proved), Everything falls back to facts::analyze. Returns an owned clone of self.facts (not a borrow) - resolve() needing &mut self while later steps also need &mut incremental for mark_touched/mark_everything_dirty made a borrowed return type incompatible with this codebase's existing pattern of one facts variable read across several subsequent step blocks before the next recompute point.

Pattern applied uniformly to every step:

Migrated final_return_temps onto the query engine as a StmtWindowRule (src/fixups/query/rules/final_return_temps.rs), rather than porting its legacy fixpoint-loop structure.

Confirmed the theory discussed before starting: the legacy Fixup found and applied exactly one `let _vN = init; return _vN;` -> `return init;` rewrite per fixup() call (early-returning after one edit), which is why it needed to run inside to_fixpoint_items_with_facts - removing a statement shifts every later statement's AstPath in that function body, so the naive one-edit-then-restart style needed fresh facts before safely looking for the next candidate. StmtWindowPlan::apply already solves this generically: it collects every matching window against one frozen snapshot, then splices multiple non-overlapping windows within the same function body in Reverse(site.start) order (stmt_window.rs's apply_body), so index shifts from an earlier removal never corrupt a later one in the same apply() call. A single plan.apply() therefore finds and rewrites every independent instance across the whole program in one shot - no fixpoint loop needed at the pipeline level. Verified empirically: the full differential suite (191 fixtures) produces byte-identical output to the old unbounded-loop version, which would have caught any case the single-shot version missed.

Added one new reusable QueryContext predicate, sole_use(window, name) -> BindingId (context.rs), proving the local named `name` defined at a window's first statement has zero writes and its only read is the window's second statement - the shape a lowered `let _vN = init; ...; use _vN` temp takes when it's safe to inline at its sole use. Added Predicate::SoleUse (proof.rs) and its predicate_name entry (rewrite.rs), and a StmtWindowCaseContext::sole_use wrapper (stmt_window.rs) per docs/writing-a-query-fixup.md's "Adding a helper" checklist. Reused the existing EvidenceDetail::Binding variant rather than adding a new one.

Found and fixed a real staleness bug while wiring the step into fixups/mod.rs: the legacy FinalReturnTemps step never needed an outer resolved-facts boundary (it computed fresh facts internally, once per round, via to_fixpoint_items_with_facts), so there was no `incremental.resolve()` call between Retval and FinalReturnTemps in the pipeline. Migrating FinalReturnTemps to read the outer `facts` variable directly means it now needs that boundary explicitly - my first pass at the wiring reused the pre-Retval facts binding, which would have run FinalReturnTemps's QueryContext against a FixupFacts snapshot stale relative to Retval's edits (exactly the hazard the incremental-facts work exists to prevent). Fixed by inserting `let facts = incremental.resolve(&program);` immediately before the FinalReturnTemps step, so it resolves Retval's mark_everything_dirty() before running - caught by inspection before running the differential suite, not by a test failure.

Migrated dead_locals onto the query engine as a StmtWindowRule (src/fixups/query/rules/dead_locals.rs), including its usage inside the shared late_loop_cleanup helper - full scope, per explicit user direction ("implement the full scope since this should be one of the trickier ones and we'll need to implement it later anyway").

Confirmed this is the genuine cascading case (unlike final_return_temps): removable_dead_local requires def_use.reads.is_empty() && def_use.writes.is_empty(). Deleting one dead `let x = y + 1;` removes one of y's recorded reads, so y can only become provably dead after that removal is reflected in fresh def_use facts - a real cross-round dependency, not just an index-shift artifact. Wired accordingly as a genuine loop (`loop { resolve -> apply -> mark_touched -> break if !changed }`) at both standalone Pass::DeadLocals pipeline steps, using the FixpointLimit::Unlimited-equivalent termination (loop until no change, same guarantee legacy fixpoint passes already relied on - each round's proof-gated rewrite narrows what's still eligible).

Added two new QueryContext predicates (context.rs): dead_local(window, name) -> BindingId (reads AND writes both empty - not the same as sole_use's exactly-one-read shape from final_return_temps) and no_effects(window) -> () (the init expression's EffectFact.effects set is completely empty). Confirmed no_effects is NOT equivalent to the existing pure() query: pure() only requires Purity::MovablePure, but dead_locals's legacy discardable_effect excludes all 10 EffectKind variants including ReadOnlyCall/VolatileRead/AtomicRead, which pure()/Purity classification does NOT treat as disqualifying (those keep purity at ReadOnly, not Effectful). no_effects is strictly narrower than "not Effectful" - its own distinct, more conservative predicate. Ported discardable_known_method/discardable_receiver (the `.len()`/`.as_slice()`/`.as_mut_slice()` structural allowlist) as plain structural checks in the rule case, matching how final_return_temps kept shape-matching out of QueryContext.

late_loop_cleanup (shared by SliceLoop/SliceReduce/RangeLoop cleanup) restructured: still runs the legacy SingletonScopes::fixup over every function first (untouched - singleton_scopes has its own separate migration ticket, .75.38), then builds and applies one query-engine dead_locals plan against the same per-round facts snapshot, `changed |= report.changed`, loops until neither produced a change. Reordering (all SingletonScopes calls, then one batched DeadLocals plan.apply, instead of interleaved per-function) is behaviorally equivalent: DeadLocals's proof for function A never depends on function B's state, and both versions use the exact same round-boundary facts snapshot, reproducing the existing (already-validated) per-round staleness/ordering behavior exactly.

Found and fixed two real, pre-existing incremental-facts coverage gaps while verifying - both latent since slate-04q.75.56.8, never triggered until dead_locals became the first migrated pass to actually chain multiple resolve() calls through mark_touched (not mark_everything_dirty) within one step:

1. def_use was never part of FixupFacts::splice_function's/purge_function_facts's maintained field set (`.8`'s original scope only covered functions/bindings/binding_types/effects/values/string_buffers/string_pointer_views/counted_loops - def_use wasn't needed by any of the six originally-migrated passes). Once dead_locals's loop spliced a function on round 2+, its def_use facts stayed frozen at whatever they were before round 1's edit - reads/writes no longer lined up with the current program. Symptom: anon_local_struct.c produced Rust with dangling `_v6`/`_v12` references to locals that were still genuinely read later but appeared to have zero reads under the stale facts. Fixed by adding def_use::collect_for_function (extracted from collect_facts's existing per-item loop, same shape as the .8.5 precedent) and wiring it into splice_function (extend, ordered after the bindings refresh since it resolves bindings by name+path) and purge_function_facts (retain).

2. borrow_alias had the identical gap - RemoveMut's binding_requires_mut depends on it. Symptom: target_stack_builtin_ops.c's `bytes` array lost its `mut` even though `bytes[0] = ...` writes to it, because RemoveMut ran against a spliced (not fully reanalyzed) snapshot for the function dead_locals had just touched, and borrow_alias in that snapshot was stale. Fixed the same way: borrow_alias::collect_for_function added and wired into splice_function/purge_function_facts.

Both gaps were caught by the full differential suite (cargo nextest r --release), not guessed in advance - confirms the suite is doing its job as the correctness bar for this mechanism, per the user's earlier direction that differential tests are sufficient verification without extra diagnostics.

Generalized CallRule to accept a FnCall<Cx> matcher struct, replacing the two hardcoded CallRule::generated()/CallRule::known() constructors.

Added rust_ast::Type: PartialEq, Eq (previously missing) - verified safe first: every field/variant in Type's definition (Prim, Custom(String), Box<Type>, Vec<Type>, bool, u64, Ident, Abi, CLibType, etc.) is already Eq-safe, no floats anywhere in Type itself (those live in Expr::Value(RustValue::Float(f64)), a different enum). Needed because Field<T,Cx>::matches requires T: PartialEq for every variant including Eq, and arg_types: Field<Vec<Option<Type>>, Cx> needs that bound transitively.

Added FnCall<Cx = ()> (src/fixups/query/patterns.rs), following the exact pattern NullaryMethodCall/LetStmtPattern/LoopStmtPattern already established with Field<T,Cx> (Any/Eq/Predicate) - but this is the first Field<T,Cx>-based matcher backed by facts/caching rather than pure AST shape:
- target: Field<CallTarget, Cx> - reuses the existing CallTarget enum (Known/Generated/Direct/Indirect) directly, so one field subsumes what generated() and known() each hardcoded separately.
- arity: Field<usize, Cx>.
- arg_types: Field<Vec<Option<Type>>, Cx> - matches against each argument's CallArgFact.declared_ty (already-collected fact via facts.call_arg_at(function, path), no new fact collection needed). None per-arg where the call's target has no known/declared signature.
- #[derive(Default)] works transparently (Field<T,Cx> already derives Default via its #[default] Any variant, verified empirically - no T: Default bound leaks through), giving the "ignore this field" default: FnCall { target: Field::eq(...), ..Default::default() }.

CallRule::matching(pass, rule, matcher: FnCall) replaces both old constructors. candidates() changed from an exact (CallTarget, arity) BTreeMap lookup to a full scan+filter: QueryContext::all_calls() (new, flattens the existing calls index) filtered by matcher.target.matches(...) && matcher.arity.matches(...) && matcher.arg_types.matches(&query.call_arg_types(call), ...) - the && short-circuits, so arg type resolution (the only non-trivial-cost check) only runs for calls that already passed target+arity. QueryContext::call_arg_types(call) is the new per-call-site arg type resolver.

Updated rules/memchr.rs and rules/libc_exit.rs to build FnCall matchers (target + arity; arg_types left at the Field::Any default for both, since neither __slate_memchr's synthetic generated target nor exit's single-int-arg signature needs type-based disambiguation beyond what target+arity already provides - the field exists and is usable by future rules that do need it, without forcing every rule to specify it). libc_exit's semantic proof body (never_returning_extern) is untouched - that decomposition is .10.2's separate scope, not this ticket's.

Verified via the full gate: cargo build, cargo clippy --all-targets, cargo fmt, cargo nextest r --release - 191 passed, 2 skipped, byte-identical output. Implemented and verified in the same pass it was created for - see description for full detail. cargo build/clippy/fmt/nextest all clean, 191 passed, 2 skipped, byte-identical differential output.

Superseded by a bigger design than originally scoped here - implemented as "Value<Cx>/Local<Cx> matchers" rather than flat no_reads/no_writes/sole_read predicates, per follow-on discussion after this ticket was created. See matcher-plan.md.

Rather than exposing three separate case-level predicate calls (no_reads/no_writes/sole_read), the usage information (reads/writes counts) moved up to StmtWindowRule's candidate SELECTION step, the same way FnCall/Definition already moved call/definition matching to selector-level Field<T,Cx> matchers (.75.56.10.3/.10.4). Concretely:

- New shared value types (views.rs): Usage { reads: usize, writes: usize }, ResolvedValue { ty: Option<Type>, usage: Option<Usage>, purity: Option<Purity> } - "what do we know about the data at this expression position," generalizing beyond just locals so the same resolver can eventually back FnCall argument matching too (not wired for args yet - no concrete rule needs it, deferred until one does).
- Value<Cx> matcher (patterns.rs): ty/usage/purity as Field<T,Cx> members, with its own matches(&ResolvedValue, &Cx) method (same shape as NullaryMethodCall/LetStmtPattern).
- Local<Cx> matcher: name/mutable/value: Value<Cx>, for StmtWindowRule's per-window binding matching.
- StmtWindowRule::matching_local(matcher: Local) (stmt_window.rs) - when set, candidates() additionally requires the window's first statement to be a Stmt::Let matching the matcher (structurally and via QueryContext::local_value, a new plain resolver: binding_type_ast for ty, def_use counts for usage, the Let statement's own EffectFact for purity).
- context.rs: dead_local/sole_use predicates removed entirely (dead_local fully superseded - "reads:0,writes:0" is now a matcher field, no case-level predicate needed at all; sole_use partially superseded - "writes:0,reads:1" moved to the matcher, but a read_path(window,name) predicate stays case-level since final_return_temps still needs the read's specific AstPath for the window-shape comparison against the return statement, which a mere usage count can't express).
- Added StmtWindowCaseContext::stmt_path(offset) - computes the AstPath of a specific window statement, used to compare read_path against the return statement's own path.

Updated dead_locals.rs (usage:{0,0} in the matcher; case body now only handles the discardable_known_method-or-no_effects branch, which genuinely can't fold into a matcher field since it's an either/or between a structural AST check and a fact-based fallback) and final_return_temps.rs (mutable:false + usage:{reads:1,writes:0} in the matcher; case body keeps the is_temp_name/returned-name/read-path-equals-return-statement checks, which are window-shape relationships, not properties of the binding alone).

Verified via cargo build, cargo clippy --all-targets, cargo fmt, cargo nextest r --release - 191 passed, 2 skipped, byte-identical output to before this change.

Replaced never_returning_extern() with an ExternFn<Cx> matcher, following the same Field<T,Cx> pattern as FnCall/Definition/Local rather than the original ticket's standalone ExternFnMatch-with-its-own-view design - kept consistent with what actually shipped in .10.3/.10.4/(unticketed Value/Local work) since this ticket was written before that pattern was established.

ExternFn<Cx = ()> (patterns.rs): name: Field<String,Cx>, arity: Field<usize,Cx>, returns: Field<Option<Type>,Cx>.

QueryContext::extern_fn(&self, matcher: &ExternFn) -> QueryResult<()> (context.rs) - NOT wrapped in the query_cache! macro, unlike most predicates: a Field<T,Cx>-based matcher can hold a boxed Predicate closure, which can't implement Eq+Hash, so it can't be used as a query_cache! HashMap key. Written as a plain method instead (same pattern already used for local_value/call_arg_types/all_calls, none of which are cached either). Scans Item::ExternBlock declarations, checks name/arity/returns via Field::matches, preserves the original's MissingEvidence-vs-Contradicted rejection distinction (saw a declaration with a matching name but wrong arity/return type, vs. no declaration with that name at all).

This predicate is now decoupled from CallRecord entirely (matches by name, not by a specific call site or the Known enum) - it's a program-level fact about a named extern declaration's shape, reusable by any future case that needs "does this named extern function exist with this signature," not just libc_exit's.

Predicate::NeverReturningExtern -> Predicate::ExternFn; EvidenceDetail::KnownExternDeclaration{target: Known, arity, returns_never} -> EvidenceDetail::ExternFnDeclaration{name: String, arity, returns_never} (decoupled from the Known enum for the same reason - a name-based matcher shouldn't require a Known identity to report evidence). Both were used nowhere else, safe to rename outright.

libc_exit.rs's case now composes: case.extern_fn(&ExternFn { name: Field::eq(Known::Exit.symbol().into()), arity: Field::eq(1), returns: Field::eq(Some(Type::Never)) })?; - using Known::Exit.symbol() rather than hardcoding "exit" as a string literal, keeping it tied to the existing Known enum identity used by the call-side FnCall matcher (from .10.3) even though extern_fn itself only needs a plain name.

Skipped ticket step 4 (CallCaseContext::require + Predicate::CallGuard): not needed - libc_exit's rewritten case has no bare boolean check left, only the one extern_fn proof call. Would have been speculative infrastructure with no current caller; add it when a real case needs it.

Found and fixed a real test coupling: tests/differential.rs's noreturn_c11_uses_process_exit_and_removes_dead_false_branch asserted on the exact old trace string ("evidence.never_returning_extern=known:exit;arity=1;returns_never=true"). Updated to "evidence.extern_fn=name=exit;arity=1;returns_never=true" matching the renamed predicate/evidence format - verified against actual `fixup-debug --debug-only-pass libc_exit` output before updating. The case name itself ("never_returning_extern", the .case() label, distinct from the Predicate enum) was left unchanged since it still accurately describes what the case proves, and renaming it wasn't required by this ticket - avoided incidental extra churn.

The query engine's rule-selection layer is now uniformly matcher-driven: CallRule::matches(FnCall), DefinitionRule::matches(Definition), StmtWindowRule::matching_local(Local), and case-level predicates like extern_fn(ExternFn) all compose from the same Field<T,Cx> combinator, replacing the earlier one-constructor-per-shape and bundled-predicate APIs. Migrated heap_ownership from the legacy Fixup trait (src/fixups/rewrite/heap_ownership.rs, now deleted) to the query engine. Modeled as a DefinitionRule over every Item::Fn candidate (query/rules/heap_ownership.rs): a single case proves QueryContext::heap_ownership_plans(definition) - a cached query_cache! predicate that ports the original plans_for_function fact-interpretation logic (filtering facts.heap_ownership by FunctionId, validating VecBuffer read-safety, resolving pointer/size/allocation/assign/free statement indices from AstPath, building realloc plans) into HeapOwnershipPlanSet/HeapOwnershipPlan/HeapOwnershipReallocPlan proof views (views.rs), rejecting MissingEvidence when a function has no qualifying plans. The case then pulls the function's current body via a new DefinitionCaseContext::function_body() accessor and passes both into rewrite_heap_ownership(body, plans) in recipe.rs, which ports the entire original AST-surgery algorithm verbatim (rewrite_body, fuse_scalar_box_initializers, the owned-pointer alias/access rewriting walk, realloc-to-truncate/resize lowering, etc.) as a typed FunctionBodyRecipe, applied via the existing replace_body() DefinitionRecipe action - no new planner or plan-diffing machinery needed. Added Predicate::HeapOwnershipPlan/EvidenceDetail::HeapOwnershipPlan{plans} for tracing. Shared default_value() between context.rs (plan construction) and recipe.rs (Box::new default arg) via a pub(super) export rather than duplicating it. Scheduling in fixups/mod.rs switched from run_once_items + mark_everything_dirty to DefinitionPlanBuilder + mark_touched(&report.touched), matching every other already-migrated query pass. docs/passes.md's heap_ownership entry describes scheduling shape (once, per function) which is unchanged, so left as-is, matching how other migrated passes' doc entries were left alone. Full gate clean: cargo build, cargo clippy --all-targets, cargo fmt, cargo nextest r --release - 191 passed, 2 skipped, including all five heap fixture differential tests (heap_box_fixup, heap_box_delayed_store, heap_vec_malloc, heap_vec_calloc, heap_vec_realloc) unchanged.

Migrated string_lift from the legacy Fixup trait (src/fixups/rewrite/string_lift.rs, now deleted) to the query engine, reusing the DefinitionRule + FunctionBodyRecipe whole-function-body pattern established by the prior heap_ownership migration (slate-04q.75.25).

Design: QueryContext::string_lift_plans(definition, recovery: &Field<StringRecoveryCandidate>) is a new plain (uncached) predicate - like extern_fn, it takes a Field matcher argument so it can't be a query_cache! key (Field::Predicate holds a non-Eq/Hash closure). It precomputes every qualifying candidate for a function directly from facts.string_buffers/facts.string_lift_plans (joined by function+binding+path, filtered through the recovery matcher), producing StringLiftPlan{path, name, ty, expr, remove_path} views - no live body traversal needed at proof time since AstPath already encodes each candidate's exact nested position. The two legacy call sites (Pass::StringLift with [BorrowedStr,BorrowedBytes], Pass::StringLiftFixupCStrings with [BorrowedCStr]) became two rule-builder functions in rules/string_lift.rs (rewrite()/rewrite_c_strings()), each hardcoding its own Field::predicate/Field::eq recovery filter inline in the case closure body - DefinitionCaseFn is a plain fn pointer (not a closure trait object), so a runtime-parameterized matcher can't be captured from an outer rewrite(pass) parameter the way dead_locals::rewrite(pass) captures pass into the RULE identity only (never into a case body).

The recipe (rewrite_string_lift in recipe.rs) ports the whole-body rewrite algorithm as a single unified recursive apply_string_lift(path, body, plans) using the same recurse-into-children-then-process-this-level order as the legacy fixup_nested-then-fixup_body, but built on the shared support::walk::nested_body_vecs_mut_with_path/with_path_segment helpers (the same ones stmt_window.rs's apply_body already uses) instead of a bespoke path tracker. This incidentally fixes a latent legacy gap: the old fixup_nested never pushed a PathSegment for Stmt::Loop/Scope/LabeledBlock bodies (only If/Else did), so string buffers declared directly inside those bodies could never match facts.string_buffers' correctly-segmented Site.path and were silently never lifted; the new implementation uses the correct segment set (LoopBody/ScopeBody/LabeledBody/etc.) via the shared walker, so that shape is now covered too - not a behavior change flagged by any test, just strictly more complete coverage from not re-deriving a parallel, incomplete path tracker.

Preserved exactly: the downstream pointer-view rewrite's two shapes - MethodCall(as_ptr/as_mut_ptr) AND Expr::ArrayPtr (array-to-pointer decay, for buffers originally declared as C arrays) - both convert to the same  cast, per the user's explicit callout that this needs to keep working for the array-decay shape, not just the method-call shape. Dropped rewrite_expr_pointer_views, a private helper in the legacy module with zero call sites anywhere in the codebase (verified by grep before removing) - not ported, since it was dead code, not a live code path. Dropped the assignment_index/remove_index >= body.len() defensive bounds check in favor of the fresh-facts-boundary trust already established for heap_ownership: same_container(declaration, assignment) preserves the safety-critical parent-prefix check (never remove an assignment from a different container than the declaration, which would silently leave an assignment to a since-immutable binding in place) but the pure staleness bounds guard is dropped since facts are always freshly computed against the exact body being rewritten within one pass invocation.

Caught and fixed a real bug before closing: initially wired the pass with a precise TouchedItems{in_place: [...]} (the pattern used by heap_ownership/string_lift/DefinitionRule passes), which broke slice_index's downstream simplification (ptr_len_slice.c and 3 other fixtures failed to compile - a stale-fact type mismatch, *mut vs *const on a downstream temp). Root cause: ptr_len changes a function's PARAMETER TYPE (raw pointer -> slice), which ripples into every caller's argument type across the whole program, the same unpredictable blast radius anonymous_structs already documented and handles via TouchedItems::unbounded() (forcing a full facts re-analyze) instead of incremental splicing. Legacy's own scheduling used mark_everything_dirty() for exactly this reason - switched to TouchedItems::unbounded() to match, verified the ptr_len_slice.c output now matches the pre-migration baseline exactly (byte-for-byte, checked via a temporary git worktree at the pre-ptr_len commit).

Design: modeled as a DefinitionRule over every function (two rule-builder fns, early()/late(), since Phase can't be threaded through a case closure - DefinitionCaseFn is a plain fn pointer with no captures, same constraint hit for string_lift's recovery-candidate sets). QueryContext::inline_temp_candidate(definition, phase) is a query_cache!-cached predicate (key: (DefinitionLocation, Phase), needed Hash added to the new Phase enum) that searches ONE function's body for the single first-eligible temp-inline candidate, replicating the legacy fixup_at/inline_nested_temps traversal order exactly (nested subtrees searched fully depth-first, statement by statement, before ever falling back to this level's own top-level statements) via a new find_inline_temp_candidate walker built on the existing immutable support::walk::nested_body_vecs_with_path/with_path_segment helpers. All ~20 pure eligibility-check functions (temp_chain_use_index and everything under it - effect/purity checks, receiver-use, option-receiver, argument type-stability, macro-arg-shape heuristics) ported verbatim into context.rs, unchanged logic, only relocated. Scheduling: preserved the exact per-round, one-candidate-per-function semantics that make this pass different from every other DefinitionRule pass so far - to_fixpoint_items_with_facts (function-by-function driver) replaced with to_fixpoint_program_with_facts wrapping one QueryContext+DefinitionPlanBuilder+apply cycle per round, which is semantically equivalent: DefinitionPlanBuilder already applies at most one edit per DISTINCT function item per invocation (all candidates found from the one shared per-round facts snapshot), matching the old run_once_items granularity, while re-deriving fresh facts.analyze() every round exactly as before - this was verified necessary (not just tidier) since a candidate's eligibility can depend on shapes an earlier-in-the-same-round edit changed. Both LateInlineTemps call sites (there are two, at different pipeline points, both unchanged code shape) and the EarlyInlineTemps call site were migrated identically; inline_temp_fixpoint_limit's round-cap for large programs (>2000 stmts) preserved unchanged at all three sites.

Hit and fixed a real gap along the way: routing the local's def-use through binding_def_use (the UseSiteRef-resolving wrapper) silently rejected every candidate because one of its reads lands in an unsafe { .. } block's tail position, whose AstPath (ending in BlockTail) use_site/self.expr cannot resolve to an expression site - caught via git-stash/pop byte-identical comparison against baseline (varargs.c and c89.c both regressed to the untouched dispatch-loop-era shape, i.e. raw __slate_va_args param plus unremoved ap alias, even though the differential suite still passed since leaving it unrewritten is still correct). Fixed generically in QueryContext::use_site (src/fixups/query/context.rs). Root cause was broader than the BlockTail symptom: facts/def_use.rs records read/write AstPaths anchored coarsely at the nearest enclosing statement/container (it never pushes an Expr(N) discriminator when descending through Assign/CompoundAssign targets/values, or through nested sub-expressions generally), while use_site's non-Stmt-ending branch routed those paths through target_expr_at_path, which expects the fully-qualified Expr(N)-marked convention used by expression_sites. That mismatch made use_site return None for any read/write whose path happened to end past a container segment (BlockTail being the case that surfaced it, but the same class of path fails for any nested sub-expression). Fix: use_site now tries exact expression resolution first (unchanged, no regression risk), and falls back to resolving the nearest enclosing statement (same technique as enclosing_statement, truncating at the last Stmt(_) segment) whenever the exact resolution fails - matching the actual precision def_use's paths support. Verified with a before/after byte-identical translate comparison across all 246 fixtures with the fix isolated (reverted just the use_site fallback, rebuilt, retranslated everything, restored, retranslated again): only c89.c and varargs.c differ, and only in the expected direction (the va_list alias now collapses, matching slate-04q.75.53's fix). va_list's context.rs now uses the standard binding_def_use wrapper again instead of the raw facts.def_use bypass, restoring proper evidence tracing; docs/passes.md entry #25 updated to drop the now-stale workaround description. cargo fmt, cargo clippy --release --all-targets, and full cargo nextest r --release (201/201, 4 skipped) all pass.

Migrated param_spills to the query engine as a single Function-scoped rule (fold_param_spills, src/fixups/query/rules/param_spills.rs). Per user feedback mid-implementation, the design was corrected from an initial monolithic context.rs fact (which manually re-walked the body for the decl statement, matched raw UseSiteRef::Statement, and read facts.def_use directly) to a version that adds ZERO new pass-specific QueryContext methods: every check composes from facts that already existed (binding_uses, enclosing_statement, statement, statement_expression, expression_place, function_bindings, function_snapshot), used the same way other migrated rules already use them. The only new addition is UseSiteRef::path() (views.rs), a two-line, obviously-generic accessor exposing the read/write site's AstPath uniformly across both variants, needed to check that a local isn't read between its declaration and the spill-store statement. Per-parameter candidate resolution and the function-wide claimed-name bookkeeping (a param can't fold into a local whose name collides with another parameter or an already-claimed local this round) live directly in the rule file as plain Rust, not as a context.rs fact, since that bookkeeping is inherently pass-specific sequencing rather than a reusable predicate. rewrite/param_spills.rs deleted (no dedicated facts collector existed to remove - legacy already only used shared facts.def_use/facts.place/facts.binding_type). The single-use check reuses binding_uses composed with a small rule-local helper (use_sibling) that truncates each use's UseSiteRef::path() down to the alias's own statement container, requiring every use resolve to the exact same sibling statement - this preserves the legacy 'confined to one consuming statement, any occurrence count within it' semantic (not a strict single-read count, since substitute_var replaces every occurrence in that one statement). The 'does the source change between def and use' recursive shape check (stmt_changes_name/expr_mutably_borrows_name/etc.) is 100% syntactic with no facts dependency, so it was ported near-verbatim into a pure helper module (src/fixups/query/var_aliases.rs), reused against the statements_between(decl, use) range (whose exclusive-both-ends semantics already match the legacy body[def_index+1..use_index] slice). Used .ordered_non_overlapping() so that when two aliases are consumed by the same statement, the first-iterated one wins this round and the second is picked up on the next fixpoint round, exactly mirroring the legacy single-shot-per-call/to-fixpoint-driven behavior instead of both getting silently dropped as a conflict.

Migrated string_params to the query engine using a Function-matched rule (query/rules/string_params.rs), not a WholeProgram/precomputed-plan recipe. context.rs gained three small generic primitives: string_param_lift_indices(function) (a per-function gate over the existing facts.string_param_lifts fixpoint fact), calls_in(function) (outgoing-calls counterpart to the existing direct_calls), and function_by_name(name). Each function's case is self-contained: it retypes only its own signature/local aliases and fixes up only call arguments in its own body, so a callee's signature edit and a caller's argument edit never share an anchor - this was required, not just cleaner, since the earlier per-parameter design produced cross-function edit sets (callee signature + caller call-site in one EditSet) that permanently conflicted with the caller's own signature edit whenever both were simultaneously liftable (e.g. a 3-level internal call chain), silently failing to lift either forever. Also discovered and fixed a real bug: the fixpoint loop must call incremental.mark_everything_dirty() (matching the legacy scheduling) rather than mark_touched(), because the cross-function string_param_lifts fact isn't recomputed by the targeted incremental splice - using mark_touched left it permanently stale and looped forever. Fixed the traced printf %c gap and, per user direction, generalized it into a broader mutation-tracking fix for printf's %s/%c constant-folding:

1. printf_macro_arg (src/fixups/query/printf.rs): %c now falls back to a runtime `(expr as u8) as char` cast when the value isn't a compile-time constant, instead of unconditionally rejecting the whole printf call. %s gets the analogous fallback: `CStr::from_ptr(ptr as *const i8).to_string_lossy()`.

2. Discovered mid-implementation that this exposed a real, pre-existing correctness bug: proven_local_c_string_arg's "is this buffer still a compile-time constant" check only recognized strcpy/strncpy/strcat/strncat as mutators (mutated_by_string_libc), so a buffer written through by memcpy/memmove kept its stale initializer value baked into the generated Rust as a literal -- confirmed on unmodified main with a minimal repro (memcpy(d, "abcd", 5) then printf("%s", d) printed "xxxx"). Verified this independently caused stdlib_coverage's memcpy/memmove probes to fail once the %c fix stopped masking it by forcing the whole call to raw libc printf.

3. Per user direction, flipped this conservative: any call other than printf taking a tracked buffer's address now marks it unprovable (strings.rs Collector, new StringBufferRejection::EscapedToCall variant), rather than maintaining a hand-written allowlist of "known" mutators. Two follow-up corrections during review: (a) initially reused this signal to block string_copy/string_lift's own rewrites of the exact strcpy/strcat calls they exist to handle -- fixed by keeping EscapedToCall out of candidates()'s blocking check, since that gates a different consumer's needs; (b) the runtime CStr::from_ptr fallback call was itself being re-discovered as "escaping" on the next fact pass, self-poisoning affected buffers -- fixed by exempting the generated CStr::from_ptr callee by name, same as printf itself; (c) the check was initially blanket "any rejection reason" instead of specifically EscapedToCall, which incorrectly picked up the pre-existing, unrelated Indexed rejection (set whenever a buffer is indexed elsewhere, e.g. `padded[4]`) and broke unrelated printf/string_lift cases -- fixed by checking specifically for EscapedToCall.

Verified: chars.c/string_lift.c/typedef_ptr_signedness.c (the originally reported %c gap) all fully idiomatize; the memcpy/memmove bug is fixed and falls back to the new runtime CStr rendering rather than either raw printf or (worse) a stale literal; string_copy_fixup.c's unrelated rewrite still fires correctly; array_init.c's s/padded lifting and const-folding are both intact. Full release suite (201 tests) passes, fmt/clippy clean.

Added assert_recovery query fixup: recognizes the libc-shim assert() macro's lowered dead-let-bound if/else{abort()} guard and rewrites it to assert!(cond), preserving the result binding as a plain let when it's genuinely still read (rare, only reachable via hand-written code shaped like the macro, not real assert() calls). Implemented as a new query-driven fixup pass (src/fixups/query/rules/printf_stream.rs, Pass::PrintfStream) registered right after printf_format. Added Known::FPrintf, extended the shared facts/printf.rs collector to also parse fprintf's format string at its offset index-1 (reusing the identical PrintfEnv-based constant-tracking and conversion-spec machinery printf already uses), and made printf_macro stream-aware (PrintfStream::Stdout/Stderr picks println!/print! vs eprintln!/eprint!). fputs targeting stdout/stderr gets its own literal-string extraction (fputs doesn't interpret %-specifiers). Both rules resolve the FILE* stream argument through the lowerer's single-use temp aliasing (e.g. let _v1 = unsafe { stderr }; fprintf(_v1, ...)) back to a bare stdout/stderr identifier, rejecting any other FILE* source (arbitrary FILE* stays on the existing libc path, matching the negative acceptance criterion). Factored the shared 'replace a call whose int result is discarded or a provably-unused let' logic out of printf_format.rs into replace_int_returning_call so all three call sites (printf, fprintf, fputs) share it. Added four differential fixtures: fprintf_stderr_with_args, fputs_stderr_plain, fprintf_stdout_with_args (symmetry), and fprintf_non_standard_file_no_rewrite (negative). Updated docs/passes.md (renumbered) and docs/README.md. Full release suite (cargo nextest r --release, 215 tests), cargo fmt, and cargo clippy --all-targets are clean.

Implemented as a new query-driven fixup pass (src/fixups/query/rules/sprintf_format.rs, Pass::SprintfFormat), positioned right after call_args and before string_lift (string_lift doesn't know sprintf writes through a pointer, so it would otherwise mis-lift the buffer as an empty read-only &str before this pass gets a chance to see the raw array form). Extended facts/printf.rs's collector to also index sprintf (format at arg 1) and snprintf (format at arg 2), reusing the exact same conversion-spec parser and PrintfEnv-based constant tracking printf/fprintf already use. Added a static worst-case-length bound (per-conversion max width, e.g. 24 digits for any integer conversion, constant-string length for %s, reject entirely for float/exponent/general since those aren't safely boundable) that must provably fit the buffer's declared capacity (or snprintf's size argument, itself resolved through the same temp/cast aliasing the lowerer introduces) before rewriting -- this was flagged mid-implementation as a correctness requirement (an unbounded sprintf into an undersized buffer is UB in C; format! has no such bound, so firing without a fits-proof would silently change the program's meaning) and is now a hard precondition, not an afterthought. The declaration + fill call collapse into a single let buf = format!(...) constructed at the fill call's position (not the original declaration's), since intervening statements -- e.g. the format args' own temp bindings -- can appear between them and moving the construction earlier would reference not-yet-declared variables. Downstream puts/printf/fprintf consumers of the buffer are reconciled (puts rewrites to println!, printf/fprintf are left alone since their own rust_string detection picks up the now-String-typed buffer once facts refresh). Buffer mutation or non-constant format after the fill correctly falls back to V0 unchanged, per the bead's explicit 'partial in-place edits' exclusion (a String can't safely represent an arbitrary raw byte write without UTF-8 validity guarantees). Added EditSet::extend to item.rs to compose independently-built edit sets (buffer decl, fill-call statement(s), each consumer rewrite) into one transactional edit. Six new differential fixtures: sprintf+puts, sprintf+printf(%s), snprintf with observed return value, non-constant format (no rewrite), buffer mutated after fill (no rewrite), and an overflow-risk case (4-byte buffer, no rewrite -- exercises the new bound check directly). Full release suite (cargo nextest r --release, 215 tests), cargo fmt, and cargo clippy --all-targets are clean.

Confirmed via emit-cir that this was an upstream ClangIR rename, not a new construct: the rebuilt clang now spells the computed-goto terminator 'cir.indirect_goto' where the prior build spelled it 'cir.indirect_br' -- same operand (a !cir.ptr<!void> loaded from a #cir.block_addr_info jump-table global), same paired cir.label landing-pad blocks. src/lower.rs already had a full handler for this shape (lower_indirect_br + block_addr_dispatch_expr, producing the __stateN = [...][idx]; continue '__dispatchN; pattern) -- it just never ran because src/cir/ir.rs's op-name match only recognized the old string. Root cause was not in Slate's weak-alias codegen itself (symbols.rs's 'core::arch::global_asm!(".weak pragma_weak_alias\n.set pragma_weak_alias, pragma_weak_target")' correctly mirrors clang's own per-TU output for #pragma weak) -- it was that this raw asm text is invisible to rustc's own #[no_mangle] symbol-uniqueness frontend check, so a same-named strong definition elsewhere in the same combined crate (strong.rs's real pragma_weak_alias fn) only collides at the assembler stage, and only if both land in the same object file. Verified #[linkage="weak"] as an alternative fails unconditionally (rustc's frontend rejects duplicate #[no_mangle] names regardless of linkage), so the raw-asm approach is the only one that can work, and its correctness is entirely contingent on codegen-unit partitioning keeping the two modules in separate objects -- which neither generated_crate_manifest (tests/support/mod.rs, used by every differential/cross_tu/chibicc harness) nor lib_crate_manifest (src/main.rs, the real translate-project --lib output) guaranteed, since neither set an explicit codegen-units and this rustc/cargo installation doesn't default to enough units for a crate this small. Bisected empirically: codegen-units=1/2 reproduce the STB_GLOBAL failure, =16 and =256 both avoid it. Fixed by adding codegen-units = 256 (Cargo's own traditional dev-profile default, well above the empirically-necessary 16 for headroom) to [profile.dev] in both manifest generators -- this is a real end-user-facing robustness gap, not just a test artifact, since translate-project --lib would hit the identical nondeterministic failure for any real C project combining a #pragma weak alias TU with a strong-override TU into one crate. Un-ignored gnu_symbol_pragmas_preserve_cross_tu_linkage. cargo fmt/clippy clean, cargo nextest r --release fully green at 212/212 (2 skipped are the pre-existing intentionally-ignored diagnostic tests).

Implemented src/fixups/facts/null_check_dominance.rs: a per-function collector that threads a 'proven non-null' set through the body (mirroring casts.rs's scoped-walker shape), recognizing two proof shapes -- (1) structured guard: deref lexically inside the non-null-true branch of an if, resolved through single-use hoisted bool temps (the '!p' -> let _v1 = !(p != null); if _v1 {...}' idiom baseline lowering produces) up to 4 hops; (2) guard-clause exit: an if whose true branch is the null case and unconditionally exits (reusing control_flow.rs's existing ControlFlowFact.falls_through, not re-deriving reachability) with no else, proving the binding non-null for the rest of the enclosing body. Also recognizes 'provably non-null at construction' (&local) per invariant 4's third accepted shape -- deliberately did NOT accept malloc() results as construction-proof despite that being my own ticket's example text, since malloc can return NULL; corrected that during implementation rather than shipping an unsound rule. A reassignment revokes an existing proof unless the new value is itself already-proven, so p = q after a valid guard on p correctly un-proves later derefs of p.

Exposed via query/context.rs::null_check_dominates(binding, deref_site) with Predicate::NullCheckDominance / EvidenceDetail::NullCheckDominance / trace formatting per the standard checklist, all #[allow(dead_code)] since there's no consuming rule yet (that's slate-04q.83.4).

Verified with a throwaway env-gated debug dump (removed before landing, not committed) against representative C: guarded deref via if(p)/if(p!=NULL)/if(!p)/if(p==NULL) all correctly proven; p->field derefs (Field-wrapping-Deref) correctly found; identity comparison p==q correctly produces no facts (out of scope here, that's .2); unconditional deref correctly rejected (no fact); deref in the wrong/null branch of an if correctly rejected; &local construction correctly proven; and critically, p=q after a valid null-guard on p correctly revoked the proof, leaving the post-reassignment deref rejected. Caught and fixed one real bug this way: Stmt::Scope (C's bare '{ }' block, which the '!p' idiom above gets wrapped in) was incorrectly treated as a proof-isolating boundary like a loop body, so guard-clause-exit proofs never escaped it -- fixed to pass proven through by &mut directly, matching how Stmt::Unsafe/Stmt::Block (equally unconditional) were already handled.

Purely additive: cargo fmt/clippy clean, cargo nextest r --release unchanged at 212/212 (2 pre-existing skipped diagnostic tests), confirming zero behavior change from adding this collector. Known, deliberate scope limits for a first landing: no && conjunct chains in guard conditions, no expression-level (ternary/match-arm) proof propagation back out of nested Expr::Block/Unsafe since expr() takes &Proven not &mut, and no malloc-result construction-proof (see above) -- all fail conservatively (reject/no fact), never over-accept.

Implemented src/fixups/facts/pointer_option_safety.rs, a per-function collector producing two independent fact families:

1. PointerOptionSafetyFact (invariants 1, 2, 7) -- one eligible:bool per pointer-typed binding. Arithmetic (invariant 1): flags any binding that is the receiver of .add()/.offset() (the only two method names src/lower.rs's ptr_stride_method_and_args ever emits for C pointer arithmetic) with a non-zero-constant argument -- .add(0) (from p[0]) is correctly exempted since it is semantically a plain deref. Int/void* roundtrip (invariant 2): flags any Cast whose target type is an integer Prim or *T pointing at Type::CLib(CLibType::Void) -- caught and fixed a real bug here during verification: void* is not Type::Custom("core::ffi::c_void") as I'd assumed, it's Type::CLib(CLibType::Void), so the void*-cast check was a silent no-op until fixed. Union sourcing (invariant 7): flags a binding whose Let-init or Assign-value is a Field projection off a union-typed base (union-ness resolved by scanning the program's Item::Record{is_union} definitions) -- caught and fixed a second real bug here: peel_casts didn't see through unsafe{ u.p } wrapper blocks (baseline lowering wraps union field reads in Expr::Unsafe), so union-sourced values were never flagged until I extended peel_casts to also peel single-tail-expression Unsafe/Block wrappers, mirroring the existing src/fixups/query/array_env.rs::peel_casts pattern.

2. PointerComparisonFact (invariant 3) -- classifies every == / != site program-wide as NullCompare (one side is a NULL literal, the other pointer-typed) or IdentityCompare (both sides pointer-typed, neither NULL), using the shared body_exprs_with_path walker for path-aware full-program traversal; anything else (mixed types, non-pointer operands, unresolvable types) is simply not recorded, so a consumer's lookup correctly rejects on ambiguity rather than guessing.

Exposed via query/context.rs::pointer_option_eligible(binding) -> QueryResult<()> (a pure gate, Err on any disqualification) and pointer_comparison_kind(site) -> QueryResult<PointerComparisonKind>, with the standard Predicate/EvidenceDetail/trace-formatting plumbing, all #[allow(dead_code)] pending the consuming rule in slate-04q.83.4.

Verified with a throwaway env-gated debug dump (removed before landing) across 9 representative C shapes: pointer arithmetic (add/offset with nonzero and non-constant args) correctly disqualified; p[0]/.add(0) correctly exempted; int and void* roundtrip casts correctly disqualified (after the CLibType fix); union-sourced locals correctly disqualified (after the peel_casts fix); identity comparisons (a==b), NULL comparisons (a==0), and unclassifiable comparisons ((long)a==b, itself also correctly disqualified under invariant 2 since it casts a to i64) all classified correctly. Confirmed the eligible flag is stable and correct from a very early point in the fixup pipeline onward (traced the full analyze() call sequence to rule out cross-snapshot FunctionId-numbering noise as a real bug).
