Implemented src/fixups/facts/struct_field_ownership.rs, a purely structural, whole-program collector operating only on program.items's Item::Record definitions (no per-function scanning needed -- deliberately scoped narrower than my own original design draft's steps 1-2/allocation-classification, which I dropped as out of scope: the acceptance criteria only tests tree/cycle shape, and allocation-site evidence composition is properly slate-04q.83.6's job to add when it actually needs a specific shape, not something to pre-guess here).

Two combined rules, both operating on a simple 'record type reference graph' built from every pointer-to-record field across all records:
- Self-reference cap: a field whose pointee is its OWN record type is tree-eligible only if it's the SOLE such field on that type. A doubly-linked list's next+prev (both *mut Node) both get rejected under this rule -- this is deliberately the same blunt rule that would also reject a legitimate binary tree's left+right (both *mut Node), which is an accepted, documented limitation per the parent epic's bias toward bailing over misclassifying, not a bug.
- Cross-type cycle rejection: a field whose pointee is a DIFFERENT record type is rejected if that type can reach back to the field's own record type through some chain of pointer fields (graph reachability, DFS with a visited set) -- covers the general parent/child mutual-reference case invariant 9 also calls out, verified with a Parent.first_child/Child.owner two-type cycle (both correctly rejected).

Exposed via query/context.rs::struct_field_ownership_facts() -> QueryResult<Vec<StructFieldOwnershipFact>>, added to the existing query_cache! macro (whole-program, key=()) alongside ptr_len_slices/anonymous_structs/etc. Extended query_cache! itself to forward  is unblocked and ready.

Implemented Pass::OptionBoxLocals: recovers Option<Box<T>> for local pointers that
start NULL, get conditionally malloc'd, and are used behind a single dominance-proven
`if (p) { ...; free(p); }` guard. Decl becomes `Option<Box<T>>`, NULL/malloc
assignments become None/Some(Box::new(...)), the guard becomes
`match p.take() { Some(p) => {...}, _ => {...} }` with the trailing free() dropped
(Drop handles it), and p==NULL/p!=NULL style checks never need touching because the
guard rewrite subsumes them. Also implemented the identity-comparison requirement:
p == q / p != q between two pointers this pass converts is rewritten to
std::ptr::eq over `.as_deref().map_or(std::ptr::null(), |r| r as *const T)` on each
side, so None/None compares equal (matching C's NULL==NULL) and Some/Some compares
by address, never by derived Option<Box<T>> value-equality.

Real bugs found and fixed along the way, including two in the already-closed
ticket .1 (null_check_dominance.rs), which had never been exercised by a downstream
consumer until now:

1. null_check_dominance.rs's guard-shape detection resolved hoisted *boolean*
   temps (`let _v1: bool = ...`) via bool_defs/resolve_cond, but not hoisted
   *pointer-value* temps -- an earlier pass rewrites `if (p)` into
   `let _v4: *mut i32 = p; if _v4 != null` before this pass runs, so the dominance
   prover was proving `_v4` non-null and never attributing that proof to `p`. Fixed
   by adding resolve_pointer_alias, which follows chains of `let x = y;`-shaped
   var-to-var aliases (stopping before fully unfolding into a literal) so the
   proof still resolves to the real binding name.
2. null_check_dominance.rs's stmt() walker never wrapped statement-root
   expressions (Let init, Assign target/value, If cond, etc.) in the
   PathSegment::Expr(N) segment that the shared walk::stmt_exprs_with_path
   convention adds, so its recorded AstPaths silently diverged from every other
   fact collector's paths for the same source expressions. Fixed by wrapping
   every affected case with walk::with_path_segment. Combined with switching
   null_check_dominance_at's lookup from exact AstPath equality to
   walk::paths_overlap, deref sites now correctly match dominance facts recorded
   at coarser statement-level granularity.
3. The generated free() call's own argument gets hoisted into a pointer-value
   temp too (`let _v11 = p; free(_v11 as *mut c_void)`), so a naive
   `is_free_call(expr, name)` check comparing the raw Var name never matched.
   Fixed by building a local alias map from the guard body's own Let statements
   and resolving through it (same pattern as #1, scoped to the rule instead of
   the fact collector).
4. The identity-comparison condition itself gets boolean-hoisted
   (`let _v9: bool = p == q; if _v9 {...}`), so a direct pattern match on the
   if-statement's cond for Expr::Binary{Eq/Ne} never fired. Fixed the same way
   as null_check_dominance.rs: resolve the condition through the function's
   let_defs map before pattern-matching.

All four were genuine "the rewrite silently never fires" correctness gaps, not
API misuse -- confirmed by dumping the exact intermediate program state right
before Pass::OptionBoxLocals runs and comparing it against what the fact
collectors were actually matching.

Scope narrower than the parent epic in a few ways, all matching the
"leave as raw-pointer baseline if any invariant fails" principle:
- Only a single guard per candidate is supported (multiple independent guards
  on the same pointer reject the whole candidate).
- Only the "starts NULL, no allocation at declaration" shape is handled here;
  pointers unconditionally allocated at declaration are heap_ownership.rs's
  territory, not this pass's -- confirmed heap_ownership.rs has its own
  pre-existing aliasing bug (`p = malloc(...); q = p;` leaves q's declared raw
  pointer type inconsistent with p's new Box type) but that's out of scope for
  this ticket since it's a defect in an already-shipped, unrelated pass.
- Identity-comparison rewriting only fires when the comparison is directly an
  if-statement's condition (possibly through one level of boolean-temp
  hoisting); comparisons used as plain sub-expressions elsewhere are left
  unrewritten (safe: those pointers just never became eligible/converted in the
  first place if they're not decl-guarded the way this pass requires).

subsequent realloc_at/pointer_alias_temp_from_any/heap_use matches on the same
pointer were still accepted and appended to `uses` with no ordering check.
Added `if free.is_some() { return None; }` guards to all three match arms
(realloc, alias, heap_use) right after the free-call arm, so any read, write,
realloc, or aliasing of the pointer found after its free() now rejects the
whole ownership candidate -- it falls back to baseline raw *mut T Rust
(preserving the same UB the C had, rather than silently resolving it).

Verified the exact baseline-lowering shape empirically before writing the
collector (via a temporary PRE_HEAP debug dump, removed before finishing):
malloc/calloc calls always get hoisted into a temp let
(`let _v3 = unsafe { malloc(...) };`) even inside a function whose C source
directly writes `return malloc(...);`, and the return statement itself stays
a literal `Stmt::Return`, not a tail expression -- so the detection shape is
"exactly one Stmt::Return anywhere in the function, found at the function
body's top level, whose (cast-peeled) expr is a bare Var naming a temp that
was itself just defined via the same malloc/calloc-call shape
heap_ownership.rs already recognizes."

Scope, deliberately narrow, matching every other ticket in this epic's
"leave as baseline/reject rather than partially handle" discipline:
- Requires the function have exactly one Stmt::Return in its ENTIRE body
  (any nesting depth) and that one return must be a top-level statement of
  the function body, not nested in any if/else/loop. A function with a
  conditional return (if (x) return malloc(...); else return NULL;) has two
  nested returns and zero top-level ones -- rejected on both counts
  independently, not specially handled.
- The return's traced temp must be the malloc/calloc call's own hoisted
  temp directly. A named local that got malloc'd then freed then returned
  (int *p = malloc(...); free(p); return p;) is rejected too, but as a side
  effect of not recognizing the indirection at all (p's own declaration is a
  NULL-decl, not a malloc-shaped let) -- not via explicit free-tracking. This
  is a real narrowing versus a fuller "track uses between allocation and
  return like heap_uses_are_owned does for the assignment case" -- accepted
  as a documented gap since the ticket's stated fixtures don't need it, not
  discovered as an oversight.

Implemented the interprocedural caller-eligibility join: whether a function

Split into two pieces during implementation, since the ticket's own acceptance
criteria (a mutually recursive pass-through pair) turned out to require the
recursion to live in a different place than the description first suggested:

1. Extended, recursive "resolved allocation summary" (new, beyond what the
   ticket description names but required by its own third acceptance
   criterion): slate-knus.1's CalleeAllocSummaryFact only recognizes a
   function whose return traces to a DIRECT malloc/calloc call. A
   pass-through wrapper (`int *wrapper(void) { return alloc(); }`) has no
   such summary at all under .1's intentionally-intraprocedural scope. Added
   resolve_summary(name, ..., visited): base case is .1's existing summary;
   recursive case is "the function's one and only top-level return is
   Expr::Call{func: Var(other_name), ..} to another user-defined function,
   and THAT function (recursively) has a summary too, which gets inherited."
   Verified empirically first (via a temporary PRE_HEAP-adjacent debug dump)
   that `return alloc();` does NOT get hoisted into a temp the way
   `x = alloc();` does -- baseline lowering only hoists call results when
   they're assigned to a named binding, not when directly returned -- so the
   recursive case matches Stmt::Return's expr directly, no temp-name lookup
   needed, simpler than the base case.

   Cycle guard: a plain visited-set (BTreeSet<String>) threaded through the
   recursion, per the ticket's design note -- NOT fixed-point iteration.
   Re-entering a function already in the set returns None for that lookup.
   Verified this resolves a genuine cycle (f() { return g(); } / g() {
   return f(); }, neither with an independent malloc) to "no summary for
   either" without hanging -- confirmed by timeout-wrapped run completing
   normally with zero eligibility facts produced for f or g.

   heap_uses_are_owned, null_pointer_decl, and assigns_allocated_pointer from
   private to pub(super)) rather than reimplementing use-classification
   logic that already correctly distinguishes safe indexed/scalar
   read-write from disqualifying raw pointer arithmetic (via
   reassigns_pointer's fallback rejection) and already requires a matching
   free() call. The only new code is finding the call-sourced allocation
   site itself (call_allocation_temp/find_call_allocation, mirroring
   heap_ownership.rs's own allocation_temp/find_allocation but matching
   "Let-bound temp from a call to a resolved-summary function" instead of
   "Let-bound temp from malloc/calloc").

Key finding, which substantially changes this ticket's scope from what the
epic's design note assumed: the multi-function atomic EditSet primitive
already exists in src/fixups/query/item.rs. An EditSet is Vec<AnchoredEdit>,
and each AnchoredEdit variant (Function/Expression/Statement/etc.) carries
its own item_index -- nothing in the type requires all edits in a set to
target the same item. The overlap checker (anchors_overlap) already compares
item_index before flagging a collision, so edits in different functions
never spuriously conflict; the per-set validation (missing_targets) already
checks every anchor in a set against the pristine program before any
mutation and drops the WHOLE set if any anchor is stale; and the appliers
(apply_function_edits, apply_statement_edits, etc.) already iterate their
edit lists independently by item_index with no single-item assumption
anywhere. src/fixups/query/rules/unused_params.rs is already-shipped,
already-tested (via its own e2e fixture) production evidence of exactly this
shape: it builds one EditSet containing a Function-anchor replacement of the
callee PLUS an Expression-anchor edit at every call site, which may live in
different functions than the callee -- proving the "callee signature change
+ N callers' edits, atomic or nothing" pattern this epic needs already works
end to end.

Given that, this ticket's actual gap was narrower than its own design note
implied: not missing engine machinery, but missing test coverage proving the
specific "Function-anchor replace in one item + Statement-anchor edit in a
DIFFERENT item, same EditSet" shape behaves atomically -- item.rs's existing
unit test suite (missing_target_rejects_the_complete_edit_set,
mixed_edits_use_snapshot_paths_and_report_one_atomic_application, etc.) only
ever exercised single-item programs, and none of them used an
AnchoredEdit::Function anchor at all (constructing a valid FunctionRef needs
a real FunctionId from facts::analyze, which the existing test helpers never
did). Function-kind edits had zero unit coverage despite being
production-used by heap_ownership.rs, option_box_locals.rs, and
unused_params.rs.

No changes needed to AnchoredEdit, the planner's overlap logic, or any

Design: wired slate-knus.1's callee-allocation-summary,
slate-knus.2's caller-eligibility-join, and slate-knus.3's proven multi-item
EditSet primitive together. New Pass::InterproceduralAllocPromotion runs
right after Pass::OptionBoxLocals (same position as heap_ownership.rs,
before Pass::DeadLocals). Reused heap_ownership.rs's existing use-rewriting
engine wholesale rather than reimplementing pointer-arithmetic-to-indexing
conversion: bumped OwnedHeap/OwnedHeapPlan/rewrite_owned_stmt (the
structural, name+kind-driven leaf rewriter that converts *p.add(i) -> p[i]
and unwraps the now-redundant unsafe wrapping as part of the same walk) and
added a new OwnedHeap::from_owners constructor so the caller-side rewrite
doesn't need to fabricate an unrelated HeapOwnershipPlan just to build one.
Did NOT reuse heap_ownership.rs's own orchestrator (rewrite_owned_body_stmts/
ownership_plan) -- it's tightly coupled to malloc/free-shaped flat
statement-index bookkeeping (pointer decl must be a top-level Stmt::Let,
calloc-count assumed at allocation_stmt-2, etc.) that doesn't fit a
call-sourced allocation. Wrote a new, much smaller orchestrator instead
(rewrite_interprocedural_alloc_callee/rewrite_interprocedural_alloc_caller
in recipe.rs) that only handles the declaration retyping and
alias/free-statement bookkeeping this shape actually needs, then hands off
to the shared leaf rewriter for every use site.

Two real bugs found and fixed along the way, both surfaced only once an
actual end-to-end fixture was run through the full pipeline (not caught by
any prior ticket's own testing, since neither .1 nor .2 exercised a real
rewrite):

1. The ticket's own required fixture -- x[0] = 10; printf(...); return 0;
   with no free(x) call at all -- was being rejected outright:
   heap_uses_are_owned (reused from heap_ownership.rs for the caller-side
   eligibility check) hard-requires a matching free() call
   (let (free_index, free_temp) = free?;), a requirement heap_ownership.rs's
   own pass genuinely needs (its Box/Vec is meant to REPLACE an explicit
   malloc/free pair) but that doesn't apply here -- the callee already fully
   owns the allocation lifecycle via Vec's/Box's Drop, whether or not the
   caller happens to free it explicitly. Made the free requirement an
   explicit require_free: bool parameter (heap_ownership.rs's own call site
   passes true, preserving its exact existing behavior byte for byte; the
   new interprocedural caller-eligibility check passes false). Also had to
   widen OwnedHeapUses's free_index from usize to Option<usize> to carry the
   "no free found" case through, and thread the resulting read_safety value
   into the caller-eligibility fact -- .2's own collector had been silently
   discarding it, but it's required to decide Vec vs Box the same way
   heap_ownership.rs's own ownership_plan does (Elements-extent with
   MayReadUninitialized read_safety must reject the whole conversion, not
   just fall back to raw pointers, matching the existing rule's own
   discipline).

2. .1's CalleeAllocSummaryFact never recorded where the malloc call itself
   lives (only the return statement), so there was no way to remove it once
   the return got replaced with vec![0; N] -- this is exactly the same
   "leftover malloc call executes and leaks" class of bug found and fixed
   earlier in slate-04q.83.4. Added alloc_source_path to the fact (the
   malloc-temp's own Let statement, already located internally by the
   collector via find_temp_index but previously discarded) and removed that
   statement as part of the callee rewrite; verified generated output has
   zero remaining malloc calls or extern declarations once nothing else
   references it.

Fixed four distinct O(n^2) sources in the fixups query engine, found via iterative profiling (SLATE_FIXUP_TIMING + perf): PlanBuilder::finish()'s all-pairs overlap check, add_rule()'s selected_sites rescan, expression_matches()'s full-body walk instead of direct path navigation, and three salsa.rs accessors (effect/def_use/bindings_read_under+written_under) doing per-call linear scans instead of memoized per-function indexes. xmltok.c improved from ~114s to ~95-100s (byte-identical output, full nextest 250/250 green). A synthetic adversarial single-function serial-dependency-chain fixture went from never terminating to ~26s at 4500 statements - still slightly superlinear (one more minor linear-scan contributor identified via perf but not chased, per diminishing returns and since real C code doesn't produce this shape). Added a bounded-time regression test for this fix specifically.

Added memoized per-function indexes (places_by_path, control_flow_by_key) replacing linear .find() scans in SalsaFacts::place/control_flow. Verified via perf (symbols no longer appear in profile), full nextest (250/250), and byte-identical xmltok.c output.

Fixed binding_type_ast/binding_name (scanned every function in the program) and binding_by_local_path (linear scan) with memoized per-function indexes. Also fixed the shared root cause, SalsaFacts::function_input, which every accessor calls and was itself an O(functions_in_program) linear scan-by-name - added a functions_by_name index. This last fix alone dropped real xmltok.c from ~95-100s to ~43.5s (byte-identical output), since it has 228 functions vs our synthetic fixtures' 1-2. Full nextest 250/250 green.

Audit complete. Found 11 hot (per-candidate) linear-scan accessors in src/fixups/salsa.rs beyond what slate-te22.1/te22.2 already fixed, plus 2 cold ones not worth chasing. Filed three child tickets ranked by expected impact: slate-te22.5 (P1, callsite/call_arg_at scan the WHOLE PROGRAM's call sites, not just the current function - likely the single biggest remaining win given how large the function_input fix was), slate-te22.6 (P1, binding_requires_mut/borrow_alias_reasons - RemoveMut pass, three layered nested scans in one function), slate-te22.7 (P2, seven smaller single-fact accessors, same fix template, bundle them). Did not audit facts/mod.rs or query/context.rs beyond spot checks - flagged as a possible future follow-up if salsa.rs's fixes don't fully close the gap.

Fixed: callsite/call_arg_at now use position-indexed lookups (callsite_index, call_arg_index on ProgramInput) instead of scanning the whole program's call sites. Correct and verified (250/250 nextest, byte-identical xmltok.c output, symbols gone from perf profile), but wall-clock impact on xmltok.c was negligible (~43.5s -> ~43.3s) - this file's callsite density apparently wasn't the audit's predicted bottleneck. Fix kept as a legitimate complexity improvement regardless.

Fixed: binding_requires_mut/borrow_alias_reasons family now use indexed lookups (borrow_alias_by_binding, reused binding_ids_by_name) instead of three layered linear scans, plus the same 'scan every function' bug fixed elsewhere. Verified correct (250/250 nextest, byte-identical output including a new synthetic RemoveMut-heavy fixture). Wall-clock impact modest (~4.5% on real xmltok.c, ~41.4s vs ~43.3s) rather than the audit's predicted large win - borrow_alias facts are sparse so the old linear scans were already cheap in absolute terms. Kept as a correct complexity fix regardless.

Fixed 6 of 7 accessors (string_buffer_at, string_libc_use, cast_at, pointer_option_safety_of, c_string_literal, ascii_numeric_string) with memoized per-function indexes. Deliberately skipped null_check_dominance_at - its paths_overlap predicate isn't exact-match, and given te22.5/te22.6 both showed negligible real-world wins from this class of sparse-fact fix, the risk of a subtle prefix-matching bug wasn't worth it. Full nextest 250/250, byte-identical xmltok.c output. Wall-clock flat (~41.4s -> ~42.2s, noise) - consistent with te22.5/te22.6's finding that these sparse per-function facts were never the real bottleneck.

Landed mimalloc (~20-24% win, kept) and an allocation-free def_use_query_path_overlaps (~3-5% additional, kept). Tried and reverted a SmallVec<PathSegment> experiment - it made AstPath 6x wider, which bloated Rejection/DefUseFact/BTreeMap-key sizes throughout the hot path and was a net loss despite eliminating allocations (PathSegment being Copy didn't save it - the cost was struct-size amplification through Result<T,Rejection> plumbing, not copy cost). Also confirmed a QueryContext-level cache for binding_uses isn't viable without breaking lifetime variance - real caching needs salsa itself. Net: ~2x faster than the pre-epic baseline on the adversarial fixture (N=4500: 25.8s -> 13.24s), real xmltok.c ~43.5s -> ~33s. Remaining superlinearity is architectural (full QueryContext rebuild every pass x round) - filed as slate-nufb, backburner.

All 7 children complete. Real xmltok.c: never completed after 10+ minutes (start of slate-xzn6) -> ~33s (end of this epic). Fixed ~9 distinct O(n^2)-or-worse fact-lookup patterns across the fixups query engine, plus mimalloc adoption and one allocation-free rewrite. Filed slate-nufb (backburner epic) for the remaining architectural cost: QueryContext gets fully rebuilt every (pass x round) instead of being salsa-tracked/incremental - the real fix once the fixup ladder grows toward the project's stated hundreds-to-thousand-pass scope.

Delivered: per-item/per-function salsa split (ItemInput, FunctionInput carrying item_index/ItemInput, BaseWalk split into per-function walk). Real measured win: 32.2/32.5s -> 27.8-28.0s (~14%) on real xmltok.c. This is the foundation slate-nufb.2's fixes built on.

Delivered several rounds of measured wins (calls/calls_by_site pilot, expression_parents algorithm rewrite - the single biggest win of the whole epic, all_binding_refs consolidation): 27.8-28.0s -> ~14.8-15.4s (>47% further reduction on top of nufb.1). Original 'migrate QueryContext fields to salsa' framing turned out to be the wrong shape for most of the win - the dominant costs were an O(depth x log n) algorithm bug and redundant whole-program aggregation/cloning, not missing incrementality. Diminishing returns hit: remaining cost is ~12% mimalloc allocation volume + ~11-13% irreducible AST walk/clone cost, neither fixable with a narrow change. Follow-up filed as slate-nufb.3 (backburner, needs its own design pass).

Fixed. Root cause: defined_functions()/defined_globals() (src/lower.rs) gated the project-wide cross-TU symbol table on externally_exported() (linkage AND ELF visibility) instead of linkage_is_external() alone, so -fvisibility=hidden functions/globals never entered the table and sibling TUs fell back to stale extern-block stubs while the defining TU stripped their 'unused' params. Fixed defined_functions/defined_globals/unsafe_defined_functions to use linkage_is_external only. Separately, a function/global's OWN pub+extern-C+no_mangle promotion still needs externally_exported() for genuinely local symbols (regression-tested by visibility_attrs_lower_best_effort/visibility_pragma_stack_controls_rust_exports, which require hidden-and-never-cross-referenced symbols to stay private) -- so added ProjectInfo.cross_referenced_functions/cross_referenced_globals (populated via new lower::declared_globals + existing declared_functions, unioned project-wide before the per-file lowering loop, mirroring the existing has_setlocale/SkipSet precedent) and OR'd it into the pub/extern-C/no_mangle decision at the 3 FnDef sites and 8 GlobalVar sites in lower.rs. Verified: tests/fixtures.library/hidden_visibility_callback/ + library_project_resolves_hidden_visibility_cross_tu_callback (tests/cross_tu.rs) now pass; visibility_attrs_lower_best_effort and visibility_pragma_stack_controls_rust_exports still pass (no regression); full nextest suite 250/251 (only the other 4 not-yet-fixed libexpat fixtures fail, as expected). Fixed. Root cause confirmed: collect_records (c_ast.rs) collects each function-local struct occurrence separately, but lower.rs folded them into records: BTreeMap<String, Record> keyed by bare sanitized name via naive last-write-wins collect(), collapsing distinct local layouts (e.g. libexpat's many per-test 'struct TestCase { ... };') under one definition -- while usage sites already correctly referenced ClangIR's own uniquing suffixes (TestCase, TestCase.0, TestCase.1 -> sanitized TestCase, TestCase_0, TestCase_1), which had no matching def.

Fix: added resolve_local_record_collisions (src/lower.rs) that, for every AST record base name with 2+ occurrences, matches each CIR-uniqued struct alias (module.aliases) back to its correct AST Record by comparing field-name sequences -- field names come from cir.get_member's 'name' attr, via a new non-anon-gated collect_local_record_field_names (generalizes the existing collect_anon_record_info/anon_alias_key machinery, which was hardcoded to anon.*/anon_*/__once_flag names only). Content-based matching was used instead of a positional/declaration-order guess because CIR's bare-vs-.0-vs-.1 assignment does NOT track AST declaration order (verified empirically: the fixture's first-declared function did not get the bare name). Matched records get their own .name field overwritten to the disambiguated key (record_lit_name derives the printed Rust identifier from record.name, not the map key it's stored under -- found via a second bug: even after the def existed, struct-literal expressions still printed the old bare name). Also added Lowerer.local_record_extras + an emission loop in lower_module, since the existing per-record item-emission loop iterates c.records's own (undisambiguated) name field and would never surface the new _0/_1 map keys otherwise.

Verified: new fixture tests/fixtures/local_struct_name_collision.c (2 functions, same local struct tag name, different field layouts) passes differential testing. Full nextest suite 250/251 (only the other 3 not-yet-fixed libexpat fixtures red, no regressions). Re-ran translate-project --lib --compile-commands against real libexpat: the 3 original cargo-check E0425 errors are gone (0 remain), E0605 14->3, panic/'error' 30->8, E0560 103->71, E0609 unchanged at 15 -- real but partial improvement, since the content-based field-name match can't resolve a collision family when CIR's get_member never touched every field of some colliding layout (no fallback attempted for those, by design, to avoid guessing wrong). Filed as known follow-up if the remaining ~71 E0560/15 E0609 warrant a second pass.

Fixed. Root cause confirmed: element_place_expr (src/lower.rs) had a guard for FLEXIBLE ARRAY MEMBERS ('unbounded', declared-size-0 arrays) that renders array-element addressing as pointer arithmetic (base.as_mut_ptr().add(idx)) instead of literal Rust indexing (arr[idx]), but no equivalent guard existed for the common C 'one past the end' bound idiom on a FIXED-size array (e.g. libexpat's siphash.h: '#define sip_endof(a) (&(a)[sizeof(a)/sizeof(*(a))])', used as a loop bound, never dereferenced). Since Rust's arr[N] on a length-N array is a compile-time-provable out-of-bounds access even inside addr_of_mut! (rustc's #[deny(unconditional_panic)] catches it before any reference forms), this produced a hard compile error instead of a differing-behavior bug.

Fix: cir.get_element's declared array length is now computed unconditionally (previously only for the global-array-literal special case) and, when the index operand resolves to a known-constant value >= that length via the existing known_arith_value/macro_arith_values SSA-level constant tracking, ElementPtr.out_of_bounds is set and element_place_expr takes the same pointer-arithmetic path as the unbounded case.

Getting there required two follow-on fixes to the constant-tracking itself, found via a debug trace against libexpat's actual sip_endof(a) pattern: (1) fold_int_arith (used by lower_int_arith to populate macro_arith_values, consumed by known_arith_value) only handled Add/Sub/Mul -- extended to Div/Rem (guarding against divide-by-zero) since sizeof(a)/sizeof(*a) is a division of two constants that never got folded, so the div's own SSA result was invisible to any later known_arith_value lookup; (2) per user request while already in this code path, also extended fold_int_arith to BitAnd/BitOr/BitXor/Shl/Shr (checked_shl/checked_shr guard against out-of-range shift amounts) and added fold_unary_arith for Neg/Not (cir.not is C's , not  -- confirmed via existing code comment and the absence of a separate CIR op for bitwise complement -- so folding via i128's bitwise Not is directly correct, no bool-vs-int ambiguity), wired into lower_neg/lower_not the same way lower_int_arith already wires binops. All of these are pure constant-folding extensions (strictly more cases resolve to a known value; never changes an already-resolved value), so risk is limited to inputs that previously silently fell through to unfolded rendering.

Verified: new fixture tests/fixtures/array_one_past_end_bound.c passes differential testing. Full nextest suite 250/251 (only the 2 other not-yet-fixed libexpat fixtures red, no regressions). Re-ran translate-project --lib --compile-commands against real libexpat: all 4 'this operation will panic at runtime' errors are gone (0 remain, was 4, part of the earlier 8 generic 'error' count which is now down to the 2 expected summary lines x2 targets).

Fixed. Root cause was in parse_c_type (src/c_ast.rs): the array-type branch used split_once("[") plus trim_end_matches("]"), which only correctly decomposes a single bracket pair. For a multi-dimensional Clang type string like "char [4][3]" the size substring became garbage that failed to parse as an integer, collapsing to CType::Array(inner, None) and losing both dimensions (rendered as a zero-length 1D array). Rewrote it to match just the first bracket pair and recurse on the remaining bracket groups, so nested CType::Array now mirrors C array-of-array semantics at any depth (verified 2D and 3D). Extended tests/fixtures/struct_field_2d_array.c with a 3D int[2][3][4] case alongside the existing 2D char case.

Also found and fixed a second bug surfaced by the new fixture: inline_temps could inline an array/field-index read directly into a println!-style macro argument even when a sibling argument in the same macro call took a mutable raw-pointer address of the same base variable, producing E0502 (fmt macros capture all args by shared reference for the whole call). Fixed in src/fixups/query/rules/inline_temps.rs with a root-variable alias check that blocks that specific inlining.

Verified: fmt/clippy clean, nextest 250/251 (remaining failure is the separately-tracked eep4.5). Real libexpat retranslation shows utf8: [[i8; 4]; 256] with zero E0608 errors (was 8).

Fixed both symptoms. Root cause: several call sites that render array literals from cached zero/const-array facts (const_arrays, const_zero_globals) hardcoded the trailing/padding-element default to a bare Expr::Value(RustValue::I64(0)), regardless of the array element type -- correct for integer element types but wrong for struct, bool, and pointer elements, producing E0308 (expected pair/attrInfo, found integer; expected bool, found integer).

Two distinct shapes hit this:
1. A fully #cir.zero-initialized local array (struct pair pairs[] = {{NULL, NULL}};) was classified into const_arrays with an empty element list in src/lower.rs collect_global, so its copy-source padded every slot with literal 0. Redirected non-integer-element #cir.zero arrays to const_zero_globals instead, which re-derives a properly-typed default via default_value_expr(dst element type) -- kept the old const_arrays/0 path for integer element types (verified via parse_cir_int_type) so byte/char-array locals (e.g. char empty[] = "";) keep their existing, already-correct literal-0 rendering (that distinction mattered: an initial version routed ALL non-.str zero arrays to const_zero_globals and broke the string_lift/string_copy idiomization fixups, which pattern-match on the literal ArrayLit shape byte arrays produce -- reverted to keep integer elements on their original path).
2. A partially-const array (bool values[] = {true, false};) lowers in ClangIR to #cir.const_array<[#true], trailing_zeros> -- only the true is listed explicitly, false is implied by trailing_zeros. Every render_array_literal_expr call site padding a partial const_array with the destination element type default now threads a type-aware default (self.default_value_expr(elem)) through the render_array_literal_expr calls in collect_global, copy_source_value, global_array_literal_expr, and lower_cast, instead of the hardcoded I64(0).

Extended tests/fixtures/aggregate_array_literal_typed_elements.c with a count_true_flags() case covering the bool array symptom alongside the existing struct case.

Verified: fmt/clippy clean, nextest 251/251 (no regressions, including string_libc_fixup/string_copy_fixup/memcpy fixtures that initially regressed and were fixed by narrowing the const_zero_globals redirect to non-integer element types). Real libexpat retranslation: doc_info now attrInfo-typed at basic_tests.rs, atNameStart/values now [true, false] bool-typed at basic_tests.rs and alloc_tests.rs, and both "expected attrInfo, found integer" and "expected bool, found integer" error patterns are gone (E0308 count 260 -> 257, remaining E0308s are unrelated to this ticket).

Fixed: address-taken project-defined functions now stay safe fn across TUs. Verified against real libexpat: 114 -> 0 eep4.6-scoped 'expected safe fn' errors (14 remaining errors are a distinct libc-extern issue, filed as slate-eep4.11).

Fixed: split_top_level/split_top_level_arrow miscounted the '>' in a '->' return-type arrow as a closing angle bracket, under-counting nesting depth for any nested aggregate containing function-pointer-typed elements (which always embed '->' in their CIR type annotation). Enough fn-ptr fields eroded the depth cushion to 0, causing a premature top-level split mid-element and shifting every subsequent field. Verified against real libexpat: ascii_encoding/ascii_encoding_ns now bit-for-bit correct (enc substruct populated with real normal_-prefixed functions, trailing isName/isNmstrt/isInvalid fields all null), and the 70 'incorrect number of function parameters'-style errors are gone (0 remaining).

Fixed the actual root cause, distinct from the ticket's original guess: eep4.1's per-file resolve_local_record_collisions was already correctly disambiguating 3+ same-named local struct variants within one file. The real bug was in main.rs's cross-module 'shared record' promotion (all 4 translate-project pipelines): any record name appearing in 2+ files got hoisted into types.rs using whichever file's shape was seen first, with no check that the shapes actually agreed -- so two unrelated function-local structs that happen to share a tag name across TUs (e.g. TestCase in both acc_tests.c and basic_tests.c) got silently merged into one wrong shared definition, and each file's own correct local definition was then suppressed. Fix: added records_have_same_shape() and require shape agreement across all occurrences before a record name is promoted to shared_records; mismatched names are excluded from sharing so each module falls back to its already-working local resolution. Verified against real libexpat: basic_tests.rs now defines TestCase/TestCase_0/TestCase_1 as 3 distinct correct structs, types.rs no longer claims TestCase, and all TestCase-related E0560/E0609 errors (86) are gone.

Root cause confirmed: cir.select (the CIR op clang emits for C ternaries) lowered its two branch operands with a plain place/value expr, so when the branches were function references (cir.get_global of two named functions), the generated if/else yielded bare Rust fn items instead of the Option<extern "C" fn(...)> that the declared/expected type requires. This produced two symptoms: (1) assigning the select's result to an Option<fn>-typed place left both arms unwrapped (Some() never applied), and (2) calling the select's result directly triggered lower_call's blanket .unwrap() on indirect-call callees (which assumes any non-direct-callee operand is already Option-wrapped), crashing type-checking with 'no method named unwrap found for fn pointer' since the arms were bare fn items, not Option. Fix: lower_select now detects when its result type is a function-pointer type (is_cir_function_pointer_type) and routes both branches through function_pointer_operand_expr (which wraps bare global function references in Some(...)), instead of value_or_place_address_expr. This makes cir.select's output consistently Option<fn>-typed, so both the assignment case and lower_call's existing .unwrap() convention now agree. Per user feedback mid-implementation, DRY'd this out: this same 'is_cir_function_pointer_type ? function_pointer_*_expr : plain_*_expr' branch was already duplicated three times (lower_store, and twice in lower_ptr_diff/lower_ptr_stride from the recent gnu-fn-ptr-arithmetic commit). Extracted a shared fn_ptr_aware_operand_expr(operand, ty, fn_ptr_fn, plain_fn) helper and refactored lower_select, lower_ptr_diff (both operands), and lower_ptr_stride's base operand to use it. New fixture tests/fixtures/ternary_function_pointer_select.c covers both symptoms (Option<fn>-typed variable assigned from a ternary, and a ternary-selected function immediately called); verified via git-stash bisection that it reproduces the exact pre-fix bug shape and passes post-fix. Verified against real libexpat (translate-project --lib --compile-commands): pre-fix 197 total errors / 150 'found fn item' / 3 'unwrap on fn pointer'; post-fix 181 total / 122 'found fn item' / 0 'unwrap on fn pointer' -- the unwrap-on-fn-pointer symptom (shape 2) is fully eliminated, and the remaining 122 'found fn item' errors were manually confirmed to be a distinct, already-tracked issue (slate-eep4.11: unsafe extern libc fns like malloc/realloc/free not coercing to safe extern C fn types), not select/ternary related. cargo fmt/clippy/nextest (253/253) all clean.

Root cause: lower_cast's match arms were ordered so two generic pointer-cast arms (result_ty.starts_with(!cir.ptr<) && operand_ty.starts_with(!cir.ptr<), and the looser operand_ty.starts_with(!cir.ptr<) && result_ty != bool fallback) both matched before the existing (correct) transmute arm for result_ty.starts_with(!cir.ptr<!cir.func<) ever got a chance, because a function-pointer CIR type string itself also starts with !cir.ptr<. So any void*->fnptr cast (including the void*-typed NULL constant compared against a function-pointer struct field, which is exactly what minicheck.c's tc->setup != NULL / xmlparse.c's info.release != NULL compile down to) fell into the generic ptr-to-ptr arm and emitted an invalid ptr as Option<extern C fn(...)> cast (E0605), never reaching the transmute arm below it. Fix: added a guard to both generic pointer-cast arms excluding the case where result_ty is a function-pointer type but operand_ty is not, so those now fall through to the existing transmute arm instead of shadowing it. Verified: minicheck.rs/xmlparse.rs (lines matching the ticket's reported spots) now correctly emit std::mem::transmute::<usize, Option<...>>(ptr as usize) instead of the invalid as cast. New fixture tests/fixtures/void_ptr_function_pointer_cast.c (a union aliasing a function-pointer field and a void* field, read back through the void* member and cast to the function-pointer type, then called) proves the fix via git-stash bisection (reproduces the exact 'slot as Option<...>' E0605 shape pre-fix, passes post-fix). Verified against real libexpat: E0605 'non-primitive cast' errors 3 -> 0, total error count 181 -> 178. cargo fmt/clippy/nextest (253/253) all clean. Filed slate-eep4.12 for an unrelated bug found incidentally while investigating (the reverse fn-ptr-to-void* cast direction silently drops the coercion entirely) -- it does not currently manifest as a libexpat compile error, so left out of this fix's scope.

Root cause: eep4.6 marked project-defined, address-taken function DEFINITIONS as needing to stay 'safe fn' (by removing them from unsafe_functions), but that mechanism only touches src::lower's function-DEFINITION lowering path. Extern *declarations* for functions with no CIR body in this project (i.e. libc imports like malloc/realloc/free) go through a separate extern_fn_signature -> ExternDecl::Fn -> unsafe extern "C" { ... } codegen path that eep4.6 never touched, and Rust 2024 edition makes every fn item inside an unsafe extern block implicitly unsafe-to-call (and thus an unsafe fn pointer type) unless explicitly marked 'safe fn'. So malloc/realloc/free -- despite eep4.6 already computing that their addresses are taken project-wide via c_abi_functions -- kept getting declared as plain (implicitly unsafe) extern fns, and Some(realloc) failed to coerce into the safe Option<extern "C" fn(...)> field type used by XML_Memory_Handling_Suite and friends. Fix: added a safe: bool field to ExternFnDecl, set via self.c_abi_functions.contains(name) in extern_fn_signature (the single signature-building fn used by both extern-decl push sites), and codegen now emits 'safe fn name(...)' inside the unsafe extern block when set. c_abi_functions already project-wide-aggregates any cir.get_global-of-a-function-pointer target regardless of whether the target is project-defined or an extern libc symbol, so no new fact collection was needed -- just wiring the existing signal into the previously-untouched extern-decl codegen path. Internal-only synthesized extern decls (long-double shims, complex-runtime helpers, the println!-flush fflush hook) default safe: false since they're never address-taken by name. New fixture tests/fixtures/libc_address_taken_safe_callback.c (a struct holding realloc/free as plain safe fn-pointer fields, called through the struct) proves the fix via git-stash bisection (pre-fix regresses to a plain unsafe extern fn decl and Some(realloc)/Some(free) fail to coerce; post-fix both are declared 'safe fn' and the assignment/call compiles and runs, matching C output). Verified against real libexpat: 'expected safe fn, found unsafe fn' errors 14 -> 0, total error count 178 -> 164. cargo fmt/clippy/nextest (253/253) all clean.

Confirmed root cause exactly as diagnosed when this ticket was filed: casting a plain function global to a data-pointer type (e.g. 'void *slot = (void *)add_one;', which CIR emits as cir.get_global(add_one) followed by cir.cast(kind=1) from !cir.ptr<!cir.func<...>> to !cir.ptr<!void>) fell through every specific Val::Global arm in lower_cast (not a string, not a const array, result_ty already starts with !cir.ptr< so the ptrtoint arm is skipped) and landed on the catch-all arm, which only knows how to decay arrays via global_array_decay_expr -- for a bare function name that returns None, so the cast was silently dropped and the SSA value stayed Val::Global(name) unchanged, ultimately rendering as the bare fn item itself (E0308 mismatched types, not even the E0605 non-primitive-cast that eep4.10 fixed for the opposite direction). Fix: added a new arm before the catch-all for Val::Global(name) where result_ty is a non-function-pointer pointer type and name is not a string/const-array/data-global (checked against self.parent.strings/const_arrays/globals/extern_globals) -- i.e. by elimination, a function symbol -- emitting a direct 'as' cast from the bare fn item to the target pointer type. Verified this direct 'as' cast is valid Rust (fn items are directly as-castable to raw pointer/integer types, unlike Option<fn> which needs transmute) via a standalone rustc check. First attempt at the guard used self.parent.known_functions (populated only for functions with a recognized 'Known' identity like libc calls) which incorrectly excluded plain project-defined static functions like add_one -- caught this by testing against a minimal repro before assuming the fix worked, and switched to the elimination-based check. New fixture tests/fixtures/function_pointer_to_void_ptr_cast.c (direct cast plus round-trip through a function taking a void* parameter) proves the fix -- bisected by temporarily disabling just the new match arm (git-stash on the whole file wasn't valid here since eep4.11's still-uncommitted safe-fn changes to rust_ast.rs/codegen.rs live in the same working tree) and confirmed it reproduces the exact bare-fn-item-assigned-to-raw-pointer bug pre-fix, passes post-fix, and matches C output (42 99). Verified against real libexpat: total error count unchanged at 164 before and after, confirming (as the ticket's DESIGN section anticipated) this path isn't currently exercised by the corpus -- fixed for correctness/completeness rather than corpus impact. cargo fmt/clippy/nextest (253/253) all clean.

Confirmed root cause with a new translate-lowered CLI command (added this session, reusing the existing lowered_program/lowered_rust helpers already used by emit-lowered-fixtures, so a single fixture's raw pre-fixup lowered output can be inspected directly): the bug is present in raw lowering itself, not introduced by any fixup/rewrite pass -- 'translate-lowered' on the new fixture showed 'h = Handlers { ..., onEvent: std::ptr::null_mut(), ... }' even with zero fixups applied, ruling out the rewrite pipeline. Root cause: render_const_value_expr (src/lower.rs), which recursively renders each field of a #cir.const_record aggregate literal using that field's own resolved Rust type, has no dedicated arm for the '#cir.ptr<null>' raw constant string -- it falls through every specific case (const_record, const_array, #cir.zero, enum-variant match, global_view, floating point) to the generic catch-all parse_cir_scalar_expr, which renders any '#cir.ptr<null>' unconditionally as RustValue::NullPtr with no awareness of the target field's type. This is a different render path from the working scalar-assignment case ('Callback cb = NULL;'), whose #cir.ptr<null> handling in materialize_expr already branches on is_cir_function_pointer_type. Fix: added an explicit '#cir.ptr<null>' arm to render_const_value_expr, before the catch-all, that renders RustValue::None when the field's type is Type::FnPtr and RustValue::NullPtr otherwise -- mirroring the existing scalar-assignment convention. New fixture tests/fixtures/struct_literal_null_function_pointer_field.c (mirrors ExtHdlrData: a function-pointer field and a plain data-pointer field, both NULL-initialized positionally) was written and confirmed failing (red) via cargo nextest BEFORE any fix code was touched, per this session's request to lead with a failing test. Verified against real libexpat: 'expected Option<...>, found *mut _' errors 91 -> 0, total error count 164 -> 73. cargo fmt/clippy/nextest (253/253) all clean. Also landed a new 'translate-lowered <file.c>' subcommand (src/main.rs) alongside this fix -- prints the raw lowered Rust for a single file with no fixup passes applied, filling a gap where only emit-lowered-fixtures (writes every fixture) or compare-effects-rust-rust (checks effect-trace equivalence, not textual output) existed before; useful going forward to distinguish lowering bugs from rewrite/fixup bugs without the emit-fixtures dance.

Root cause confirmed: a project function's own declared return type always mirrors CIR's enum-erased integer representation (CIR never preserves enum names on a function's own signature), while a function-pointer-typed struct field's declared return type is resolved via c_ast Record facts, which DO preserve the real enum name. This meant Some(epilogProcessor) (extern C fn(...)->u32) could never coerce to the field's real Option<extern C fn(...)->XML_Error> type. First attempt (changing the function's OWN declared return type to match) caused a severe regression when verified against real libexpat (73->556 errors), because XML_Error/XML_Status-returning functions like XML_Parse/XML_GetErrorCode are pervasively called elsewhere with results captured into u32-typed locals matching the ORIGINAL C source's own loose typing -- reverted. Correct, narrowly-scoped fix (per user design discussion): leave every function's own declared signature untouched everywhere, so zero blast radius on other call sites. At the specific coercion point (assigning a bare project function to a differently-typed function-pointer slot, both via direct struct-field stores and via static const-aggregate initializers), synthesize a small safe wrapper function that calls the original untouched function and converts its return value via a newly-generated 'impl From<u32> for EnumName' (exhaustive match over known variants, unreachable!() for out-of-range -- confirmed via user sign-off since the value only ever originates from the enum's own C function). No unsafe/transmute needed anywhere. Required extending ImplBlock's trait_ field from a closed StdTrait enum to a new TraitRef{Std(StdTrait), From(Type)} to support a generic, type-parameterized trait impl (updated 4 existing StdTrait construction sites plus 2 render/key call sites in codegen.rs/directive_translate.rs). New fixture tests/fixtures/enum_return_type_function_pointer_field.c (function-pointer struct field assigned two different enum-returning functions, called through the field for side effects, avoiding a separate not-yet-fixed indirect-call-result-materialization bug filed as eep4.17) verified failing before the fix (git-stash bisected) and passing after, matching C behavior. Verified against real libexpat: 'expected fn pointer ... found fn item' errors (the ticket's core measured symptom) 54 -> 0; total error count 73 -> 19 with zero regressions. The remaining 19 errors are: eep4.15 (5, pre-existing, filed), eep4.16 (3, pre-existing, filed), and two NEW follow-ups filed from this investigation -- eep4.17 (indirect call through an already-correctly-enum-typed fn-pointer field still materializes its result via CIR's raw type) and eep4.18 (local variables explicitly declared as a named enum type in the C source still render as the underlying integer, since c_ast has no local-VarDecl-type fact collection, only Function.ret and Record field types). Both are genuinely separate root causes from this ticket's fn-pointer-coercion mechanism, not partial fixes of the same bug. cargo fmt/clippy/nextest (253/253) all clean.
Fixed pointer-to-function-pointer typedef collapse in parse_c_type; verified against real libexpat (5 -> 0 target errors)

Root cause: lower_cast's local-array-decay branch skipped the target-type cast whenever the CIR cast's result was any pointer type, so &array_var passed to a differently-typed pointer param (e.g. void*) kept the array's raw element-pointer type. Fixed to only skip the cast when the array's element type already matches the target pointee; added a secondary function_param_types-based cast fallback in lower_call for direct calls whose callee param is void* and CIR omits an explicit cast. Verified against real libexpat (3 -> 0 target errors).

Added c_ast fact collection (Function.local_enum_decls, from local VarDecl nodes typed as a named enum) and wired it into lower_alloca to override the alloca's Rust type from the CIR-erased integer to the named enum. Extended coerce_store_value and lower_load's existing member-field enum cast-down logic to also key off slot_types (not just member_ptrs), so stores into and loads from these now-enum-typed locals correctly convert to/from the erased scalar at each use site, matching the pre-existing struct-field convention. Updated the unused_type_definitions_are_pruned_but_reachable_ones_survive test whose old assertion checked for the buggy pre-fix output shape. Verified against real libexpat: the named-local-decl-typed-as-u32 pattern is gone; residual similar-looking errors are from a separate, pre-existing, confirmed-unrelated bug (array-indexed struct field access losing enum type), filed as slate-eep4.19.

Added FunctionLowerer.loaded_field_types (SSA value id -> Type::FnPtr), populated in lower_load whenever a member/slot field load resolves to an enum-returning function pointer. lower_call's indirect-call branch now threads the callee operand through this map: when found, materializes the call result using the field's real return type (via new materialize_expr_as helper) instead of CIR's erased op_result_type, fixing 'let _vNN: u32 = ...indirect_call...;' mismatches. Also extended store_function_pointer_value to transmute a fn-ptr value into its target's enum-returning shape when the stored value is not a direct named-function reference (e.g. a cir.select choosing between two functions feeding a struct field store), covering the xmlparse.rs:7541-style select-then-store pattern from the acceptance criteria. member_field_type (src/lower.rs) resolved a field-access base's record type via slot_types (plain local) or member_ptrs (nested struct field) but never checked element_ptrs, so array[i].field on a locally-scoped struct array fell through to member_field_type_from_op's CIR-type-string lookup, which failed to recognize the field's declared enum type. Added an elem_ty: Option<Type> to ElementPtr (computed from cir.get_element's own result type, same as the existing global-array-literal path already computed inline) and wired it into member_field_type as a third fallback alongside slot_types/member_ptrs. Verified against real libexpat: all 4 target errors gone (13 -> 9 total remaining before eep4.17's cleanup already dropped some; final count 2, both from the separately-tracked eep4.20).

Root cause was NOT lower_call's argument-cast logic at all (though widened function_param_types/loaded_field_types lookups there for indirect calls, via new per-parameter loaded_field_types registration at function entry, to generalize eep4.17's enum-only tracking to any fn-ptr-typed value) -- the actual bug was in lower_cast's fallback for casting the address of a KNOWN Rust global (e.g. XML_SetUserData-style static-local char) that isn't an array: it fell through global_array_decay_expr (array-only) straight to an unmodified Val::Global passthrough, silently dropping the cir.cast's pointer-type reinterpretation entirely. Fixed by materializing an explicit Cast{AddrOf{Var(sanitized_name)}, target_ty} in that fallback. First attempt routed through pointer_operand_expr/store_address_expr, which incorrectly derefs over-aligned globals (breaking the chibicc alignof test, since deref-through-a-mutable-static requires unsafe); switched to a direct AddrOf matching the codebase's existing pattern for the same shape. Part 1 (already landed): CallTarget::Generated now included alongside CallTarget::Direct in reachable_c_abi_functions's callers-of index, so the enum-coercion wrapper (__slate_enum_wrap_X) and the function it wraps correctly propagate C-unwind status to each other.

Part 2 (this session): added functions_with_cunwind_indirect_calls (src/fixups/query/rules/setjmp_recovery.rs), wired into both flip_unwind_abi_single_program and propagate_unwind_abi_across_project's fixed-point seed loops. For each function, walks its body (via walk::body_expr_any) for CallBinding::Indirect calls, resolves the callee expression's function-pointer shape (through local let-bound variables, function parameters, global static/const declarations, and struct/record field types by name -- unwrapping Option/Ref/Ptr/Complex wrappers, MethodCall/MethodCallGeneric receivers, and Unsafe/Block tail expressions along the way), and adds the function to the next iteration's seeds if that shape is already in the current C-unwind shape set. This makes a function that calls an already-C-unwind-typed function pointer *indirectly* (e.g. contentProcessor calling doContent, which calls (*parser).m_characterDataHandler.unwrap()(...)) become C-unwind itself, and -- since it's now a seed -- lets the existing backward callers-of walk propagate further up to ITS callers too.

Root cause was a missing bare-!cir.f80 case in cir_type_to_ctype (types.rs), not an AST/CIR anon-struct name collision. Fixed with one line; mix() repro now passes end-to-end. Exhaustively searched the full test corpus for genuine shape collisions under the or_insert_with merge and found none.

Fixed. lower_const's final fallback (src/frontend/lowerer/storage.rs) hardcoded Expr::Value(RustValue::I64(0)) for any unrecognized cir.const value (e.g. #cir.poison for an empty struct, emitted when a call's result is ABI-classified as Ignore/void). For a record-typed result this produced 'let _v1: raw_spinlock_t = 0;', a type error. Fixed by falling back to self.parent.default_value_expr(&rust_ty) when the result type is Type::Custom (a record), reusing the existing zero-value-struct-literal machinery instead of a bare int literal. zero-struct-2 now translates, compiles, and matches C.

Fixed all 7 cases via two root-cause fixes:

1. Alignment tracking for record-typed "coerce" ABI-bridging locals. type_alignment()
   (src/frontend/lowerer.rs) returned a hardcoded 1 for any Type::Custom (record) because
   it has no field layout to consult, so every caller comparing a CIR-supplied alignment
   against it explicitly excluded Type::Custom from the over-alignment check
   (`!matches!(ty, Type::Custom(_))`), meaning a record-typed local was NEVER wrapped to
   satisfy a higher CIR-declared alignment. Added effective_type_alignment(), which looks
   up the record's true natural alignment via the existing record_natural_align() (used
   elsewhere for sizeof/alignof), and wired it into the two real call sites (the standalone
   alloca path in storage.rs, and collect_global in lowerer.rs -- the alloca-group path
   never sees Custom types, already filtered out upstream). Fixes 20021118-1, 20040703-1,
   921123-2, 950628-1, 990525-1, pr57130, and (as a byproduct, since it also affects
   over-aligned globals) pr22141-2 plus unblocked 4 more previously-unsupported fixtures
   (20010518-2, 20050215-1, 20090113-1, pr44164).

2. bitint::{BInt,BUint}<N,LIMBS> wrapper types are always u64-limb-backed (align 8)
   regardless of the requested bit width N, but CIR's own alignment for the coercion
   buffer reflects the *natural* C representation (e.g. align 4 for a 24-bit-in-one-
   eightbyte coercion), which can be narrower. Reading such a buffer through a reinterpret
   pointer cast to a bitint type was therefore doing a plain (aligned) dereference on a
   pointer the wrapper type's own alignment requirement disallowed. Fixed by routing loads
   whose CIR result type maps to a bitint::{BInt,BUint} generic through
   std::ptr::read_unaligned instead of a plain deref, in lower_load's fallback branch
   (src/frontend/lowerer/storage.rs). Fixes 931004-11.

3. Found and fixed a third, related gap while verifying #1 against the wider corpus:
   address_expr()'s global branch (src/frontend/lowerer/storage.rs) built
   std::ptr::addr_of_mut!(*global) for any over-aligned static/global (now correctly
   Aligned<>-wrapped per fix #1) without wrapping the expression in unsafe, even though
   dereferencing through the Aligned wrapper's Deref impl requires it (unlike a bare
   addr_of_mut!(global), which the macro exempts). This surfaced as a regression on
   pr22141-2 while re-verifying the full suite -- now fixed alongside the others.
